breaking.bfsi_impact: A major Japanese brokerage has exposed the email addresses of up to 1.13 million prospective account holders plus 1,592 identity-verification document images, including driving licences, My Number card fronts and selfies — prime material for phishing and identity fraud targeting Japanese investors. Account numbers and passwords were not in the affected system, so direct account-takeover risk is limited, but firms should warn staff and customers about contact purporting to come from Monex and treat the leaked addresses as active phishing targets.
breaking.headline: Monex Securities discloses breach; up to 1.13 million email addresses and 1,592 ID document images may have leaked
breaking.known: Monex Securities announced on 13 November 2026 that a third-party system used for managing online account applications was hit by unauthorised access, and that personal data held in it may have leaked. The intrusion attempt was detected by the external operator on 18 October and external access to the system was cut off on 19 October; parts of the online account-opening service remain suspended. Confirmed as possibly leaked: up to 1.13 million email addresses registered from 16 October 2019 onward as the first step of an online account application (including duplicates, incomplete entries and people who never completed opening an account), and 1,592 identity-verification document images submitted by photo-based applications, including My Number card fronts, driving licence fronts and backs, and selfies. Monex said the My Number itself (on the card reverse) was not confirmed leaked, and that account numbers, login passwords and trading passwords were stored in a separate core system and were not exposed. No fraudulent transactions or misuse of the data had been reported as of the announcement; a forensic investigation with an external specialist is continuing.
breaking.source_name: Monex Securities announcement, 13 November 2026 (in Japanese, via PR Times); TokyoReporter, 14 November 2026, reporting Jiji Press
breaking.summary: Japanese brokerage Monex Securities said on 13 November 2026 that unauthorised access to a third-party account-opening system may have exposed up to 1.13 million email addresses and 1,592 identity-verification document images, including driving licences and My Number card fronts. Account numbers and passwords were in a separate system and were not exposed; no fraudulent transactions had been reported.
breaking.type: Named BFSI victim — major data breach
breaking.unknown: The attacker, the entry route and the exact number of individuals affected have not been disclosed; the 1.13 million figure is a maximum count of email addresses, including duplicates and incomplete applications, not a confirmed count of exposed individuals. Which of the 1,592 document images were actually taken has not been individually identified. Whether the data has been published or misused is not yet known.

breaking.bfsi_impact: Brazil's largest state-owned banking group's insurance and pensions arm has lost its full customer registration base, creating large-scale identity-fraud and phishing exposure for 7.6 million people: firms with Brazilian exposure should warn customers and staff about contact purporting to come from Caixa, and treat names plus CPFs as active impersonation material. The exclusion of bank data and passwords limits direct account-takeover risk, but CPFs are the key identifier for fraud in Brazil.
breaking.headline: Caixa Vida e Previdência discloses cyberattack; registration data of 7.6 million customers copied
breaking.known: Caixa Seguridade disclosed the incident in a market notice filed with Brazil's securities regulator, the CVM, on 12 November 2026. The attack was detected on 6 November: unauthorised access to Caixa Vida e Previdência's systems and copying of personal and registration data outside its technology environment. The affected database holds the registration records of all 7.6 million active customers plus former customers; the company did not say exactly how many individuals' data was effectively exposed. Confirmed exposed so far: names and CPFs (Brazilian tax IDs), and in part of the records addresses, telephone numbers, email addresses and dates of birth. Preliminary analysis found no indication that financial or authentication data was compromised — policy values, pension balances, bank data and passwords. The company said the incident was promptly identified and contained, that a forensic investigation with a specialist consultancy is under way, and that it notified Brazil's data-protection authority, the ANPD, on 11 November. Affected customers are being contacted by email. Caixa's Pix service had unrelated instability on 12 November; no link to the attack has been established.
breaking.source_name: Olhar Digital, 12 November 2026 (translated from Portuguese); Tecnoblog, 12 November 2026 (translated from Portuguese)
breaking.summary: Caixa Vida e Previdência, the insurance and pensions arm of Brazil's state-owned Caixa group, said on 12 November 2026 that attackers copied its customer registration database, covering all 7.6 million active customers plus former customers. Names and CPFs (Brazilian tax IDs) were exposed, with addresses, phone numbers, emails and birth dates in part of the records. The company said preliminary analysis found no sign that policy values, pension balances, bank data or passwords were compromised, and no evidence the data has been published or misused.
breaking.type: Named BFSI victim — major data breach
breaking.unknown: The attacker, the entry route and the number of former customers in the copied database have not been disclosed. The 7.6 million figure is the size of the active-customer base in the affected database, not a confirmed count of exposed individuals. Whether the copied data has been or will be published or misused is not yet known.

breaking.bfsi_impact: Japanese securities firms and banks that run or rely on stockholding-association administration should check whether their own systems share the same exposure, and treat the leaked member data — names, addresses, holdings and account details — as phishing and impersonation material: affected members should be warned about contact purporting to come from SMBC Nikko or their employer about their holdings. The incident is the third disclosure in a week from SMBC Group companies, so firms should also review whether group-wide or shared-service weaknesses are in play. There is no trading impact: the affected system cannot execute share trades.
breaking.headline: SMBC Nikko Securities discloses breach of employee stockholding-association system; up to 56,487 members' data may have leaked
breaking.known: SMBC Nikko Securities announced on 11 November 2026 that its system for administering employee stockholding associations (mochikabu-kai) — used to run the share-purchase schemes of listed companies — suffered unauthorised access by a third party, and personal data of up to 56,487 members may have leaked. The firm detected an anomaly on 7 November, confirmed the unauthorised access on 9 November, blocked access and temporarily suspended the service the same day; its investigation then confirmed the leak. The data leaked or possibly leaked includes stockholding-association names, investment holdings, member identification numbers, names, addresses, dividends and taxes, shareholding balances and transfer-destination account information — though the fields vary by association and not every member had every field exposed. Telephone numbers and email addresses were not registered in the system and did not leak. The system cannot execute share trades, so no unauthorised trading is possible through it. The company said no secondary harm had been confirmed at the time of disclosure, that it would contact affected associations individually, and warned members to beware of suspicious contact. The disclosure was published by NHK at 15:34 JST (14:34 SGT) on 11 November — in the 12:00-16:00 window — but was missed by the 16:00 wire check and picked up by this check; it is a separate incident from the SMBC Consumer Finance breach of 5 November and the SMBC email-contractor leak, involving a different SMBC Group company and system.
breaking.source_name: NHK, 11 November 2026 (translated from Japanese); TV Asahi (ANN), 11 November 2026 (translated from Japanese); Kyodo News, 11 November 2026 (translated from Japanese)
breaking.summary: SMBC Nikko Securities said on 11 November 2026 that unauthorised access to the system it uses to administer employee stockholding associations may have leaked personal data of up to 56,487 members. The firm detected an anomaly on 7 November, confirmed the access on 9 November and stopped the service the same day. Leaked or possibly leaked data includes names, addresses, holdings, dividends and transfer-destination account details; phone numbers and email addresses were not held in the system. No secondary harm had been confirmed at disclosure, and the system cannot execute share trades. This is a separate incident from the SMBC Consumer Finance breach (5 November) and the SMBC email-contractor leak — a different SMBC Group company and system.
breaking.type: Named BFSI victim — major data breach
breaking.unknown: The attacker and the entry route have not been disclosed; the investigation is ongoing. The 56,487 figure is a maximum — the fields leaked vary by stockholding association, and not every member had every field exposed. Whether any of the leaked data has been misused beyond the confirmed leak is not yet known.

breaking.bfsi_impact: Korean banks, insurers and securities firms should treat the leak as a targeting and impersonation risk: the exposed material is administrative forms and staff contact details from the evaluation process — the FSI says no vulnerability-assessment results, system diagrams or customer sensitive credit information were in the system — which could still be used to pick follow-on targets or to craft convincing impersonation of the FSI or regulators. Firms should check what they submitted through the evaluation system, watch for phishing citing the FSI or the evaluation process, and review whether staff contact details in the leaked documents need resetting. The breach of the sector's own security overseer — in the middle of a wave of 40 incidents at 37 firms — also raises the stakes for the FSC's sector-wide inspections.
breaking.headline: South Korea's Financial Security Institute hacked; financial firms' security-assessment data leaked
breaking.known: The Financial Security Institute (FSI), the Financial Services Commission-affiliated body that oversees cybersecurity for South Korea's financial sector, detected on 9 November that its 'information-security continuous evaluation' site had been hacked and reported it to the Financial Services Commission and other authorities; access was blocked. The system supports security-state evaluations of financial firms — about 3,000 firms were in scope for this year's evaluation, per an FSI press release in April — and the leaked material is assessment-support documents submitted by firms, with some personal information contained in those documents also exposed, including email addresses according to the Seoul Economic Daily. The FSI has notified individual financial firms of the leak. The site now shows a notice saying the server is temporarily suspended for service reorganisation. Financial authorities said the breach of the body that monitors financial-sector security must be treated seriously for trust reasons and have demanded a thorough check and measures to prevent recurrence. No hack of the Financial Services Commission or the Financial Supervisory Service has been reported. On 10 November the FSI quantified the leak (reported by Digital Daily, 10 November 22:58, and Seoul Shinmun, 11 November print edition): about 200 administrative forms, about 300 personal-information items (names and dates of birth contained in the forms) and about 350 masked system-user records; Seoul Shinmun reported material from 30-40 of the roughly 3,000 firms in scope leaked. The FSI said the system collects administrative forms only and holds no vulnerability-analysis evaluation results, system diagrams, resident registration numbers or customer sensitive credit information, and that it reported the incident to the Financial Services Commission and the Korea Internet & Security Agency (KISA). On 11 November the FSI confirmed the affected firms number 48, all of them mutual-finance institutions — local agricultural cooperatives, credit unions and forestry cooperatives — with no large firm and no institution from another financial sector affected; this supersedes the earlier press estimate of 30-40 firms. The leaked files number about 130. The attack used a fake account with Financial Supervisory Service-level privileges created by exploiting a flaw in the FSI's authorisation process; no actual FSS account or account information was compromised. All 246 IP addresses used in the attack were domestic Korean addresses (revised up from 236 on 13 November), none overlapping with IPs from previously known hacking attempts, and the attacker rotated through hundreds of IPs, with the attack concentrated on the afternoon of 9 November (about 13:00-14:00) before the FSI blocked access at 14:19. The Financial Services Commission began an on-site inspection at the FSI on the morning of 11 November, with FSS staff assisting, and the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency's cyber investigation unit has opened an investigation after the FSI asked police to trace the attack IPs. The FSI has cancelled the VIP event for its FISCON 2026 financial information-security conference, which had been scheduled for 12 November. On 12 November the Dong-A Ilbo reported that about 850 records containing personal information had been exposed — a higher count than the FSI's earlier estimate of about 300 personal-information items, and the two figures have not been reconciled — and that the assessment system had already been flagged in a 2022 Financial Services Commission special audit as vulnerable to data leaks; the FSI apologised for the breach. The Financial Services Commission's on-site inspection at the FSI, begun on the morning of 11 November, continued on 12 November. (Dong-A Ilbo, 12 November 2026; Herald Business, 12 November 2026) On 12 November FSI president Park Sang-won publicly apologised in person at the opening of the FISCON 2026 financial information-security conference in Seoul, pledged a full inspection of all FSI systems and fundamental measures to prevent recurrence, and said the institute was still determining whether additional data had leaked; the conference went ahead as scheduled with its VIP events cancelled. (NoCut News, 12 November 2026; SBS, 12 November 2026) On 12 November the Financial Services Commission said it would open a special audit of the FSI from 16 November, with experts and related agencies taking part. (Newsis, 12 November 2026, translated from Korean; etoday, 12 November 2026, translated from Korean) On 13 November the Financial Services Commission released a detailed timeline to the National Assembly (reported by Yonhap via Maeil Business Newspaper, 13 November 2026, translated from Korean): the FSI detected abnormal access at 10:50 on 9 November, confirmed a webshell attack at 13:54 that failed because of file-encryption policy, detected an unauthorised login attempt at 14:11, stopped the service at 14:19 and confirmed the data leak at 15:50; the initial investigation ran 15:58-23:05 that day, an emergency committee met at 13:30 on 10 November, the FSC was notified at 14:41 and a formal incident report filed at 15:48, the Personal Information Protection Commission was notified at 21:45 on 11 November, and all 246 attack IP addresses were blocked on 12 November. The attack used an SMS-authentication bypass vulnerability in normal member registration to create a fake account, then exploited insufficient access-permission verification in the evaluation system's operator check function to download files. All 246 IPs were domestic Korean addresses; the authorities cautioned that some IPs cannot be attributed to a country and that a Korean IP does not rule out routing through proxies. The Financial Supervisory Service issued a consumer warning on 12 November about voice phishing impersonating community centres and financial institutions. (Maeil Business Newspaper, 13 November 2026, translated from Korean; Woman Economy, 13 November 2026, translated from Korean)
breaking.source_name: Yonhap, 10 November 2026 (translated from Korean); Seoul Economic Daily (English), 10 November 2026; Digital Daily and Seoul Shinmun, 11 November 2026 (translated from Korean); Yonhap, 11 November 2026 (translated from Korean); Herald Business (English), 11 November 2026; Dong-A Ilbo, 12 November 2026; Herald Business, 12 November 2026; NoCut News, 12 November 2026; SBS, 12 November 2026; Newsis, 12 November 2026 (translated from Korean); etoday, 12 November 2026 (translated from Korean); Maeil Business Newspaper, 13 November 2026 (translated from Korean); Woman Economy, 13 November 2026 (translated from Korean)
breaking.summary: South Korea's Financial Security Institute (FSI), the Financial Services Commission-affiliated body that oversees cybersecurity for the country's financial sector, said on 10 November 2026 that its information-security continuous-evaluation site was hacked. The system supports security-state evaluations of financial firms, and assessment-support documents submitted by firms leaked, with some personal information in those documents possibly exposed. The institute detected the intrusion on 9 November, blocked access and reported it to the Financial Services Commission and other authorities. The incident comes amid a wave of breaches across Korean financial firms — the FSC said on 5 November that 40 incidents had been reported at 37 firms.
breaking.type: Named BFSI victim — sector security body breached
breaking.unknown: The attacker's identity is still unknown, and whether the FSI itself was specifically targeted — rather than hit opportunistically — is still an open question raised by Korean press. The leak scope (about 130 files, about 200 administrative forms, about 300 personal-information items and about 350 masked system-user records) is still described as estimated, not final. The FSI's 10 November statement quantified about 300 personal-information items leaked, superseding the earlier line reported by Yonhap that no personal information had leaked; the Seoul Economic Daily and MoneyToday had reported personal data, including email addresses, exposed.

breaking.bfsi_impact: Peer brokerages and banks in South Korea should treat the wave of attacks on financial firms as ongoing: the same pattern — abnormal external access to web-facing login and internal systems — has now hit a major brokerage days after the regulator disclosed 40 incidents at 37 firms. Firms should review web login and groupware access controls, watch for phishing and impersonation using the exposed employee contact details and customer account numbers, and check whether staff credentials need resetting given the encrypted passwords exposed.
breaking.headline: Mirae Asset Securities discloses breach of 3,800 customer account numbers and 35,255 employee records
breaking.known: The firm said abnormal external access was detected on 4 November against its mobile-web phone-authentication login service and on 5 November against its internal groupware system (mi-global); the access routes were blocked immediately and an emergency response was activated. About 3,800 customers' account numbers were exposed; the firm says no account-holder names or other sensitive customer information leaked with them. Personal data of 35,255 current employees, retirees and outsourced staff was also exposed, including names, employee numbers, email addresses, mobile phone numbers and encrypted passwords. Resident registration numbers, passport numbers, driver's licence numbers and other unique identifiers were not exposed. The firm's co-CEOs apologised in a public notice. The incident was reported to the Financial Services Commission, the Financial Supervisory Service and the Personal Information Protection Commission. The disclosure follows a wave of breaches across South Korean financial firms — the FSC said on 5 November that 40 incidents had been reported at 37 firms — and is a separate incident from the 28 October Mirae Asset Global Investments disclosure, which involved a different entity and no customer data. Newspim reported on 7 November that this is the fourth intrusion in the Mirae Asset Group in recent weeks, after customer data leaked from Mirae Asset Life on 26 October and intrusion attempts at Mirae Asset Asset Management on 28 October and Energy Infrastructure Asset Management on 2 November; the firm has not said the incidents are linked. Separately, on 12 November South Korea's Ministry of Economy and Finance said it had begun a full review of the hacking of the Government Fund Investment Pool website run by Mirae Asset Global Investments — the 28 October incident — after undisclosed data including fund returns on tens of trillions of won in state funds was taken and personal data of about 331 users, mostly public officials and public-institution staff, leaked; the ministry's Fund Asset Management Policy Committee will meet on 13 November to establish the details. (NoCut News, 12 November 2026, translated from Korean)
breaking.source_name: AlphaBiz, 7 November 2026 (translated from Korean); Korea Times, 7 November 2026; NoCut News, 12 November 2026 (translated from Korean)
breaking.summary: Mirae Asset Securities, one of South Korea's largest brokerages, said on 7 November 2026 that external attacks on 4–5 November exposed the account numbers of about 3,800 customers and personal data of 35,255 current and former employees and contractors, including names, employee numbers, email addresses, mobile phone numbers and encrypted passwords. The firm says no malware infection or service disruption occurred, no financial loss has been confirmed, and its main systems are operating normally. The incident was reported to the Financial Services Commission, the Financial Supervisory Service and the Personal Information Protection Commission.
breaking.type: Named BFSI victim — major data breach
breaking.unknown: The attack method and the attacker's identity are undisclosed, and the firm has not said how the attackers reached the two systems. Whether the exposed account numbers or employee data have been misused has not been reported.

breaking.bfsi_impact: Malaysian banks and APAC peers should watch for a formal statement from Bank Rakyat and for any leaked data sample, and warn customers against phishing that cites the incident. The claim of internal access, if true, would make this a breach rather than a defacement; until the bank confirms or denies it, treat the internal-access claim as unconfirmed and the website defacement and outage as confirmed.
breaking.headline: Bank Rakyat website defaced by actor claiming internal access; bank confirms outage
breaking.known: Pages on the bank's official web portal, including informational pages on personal financing, were briefly defaced on the evening of 6 November; the defacement was first reported on social media and the pages were restored within about an hour. The defacement notice read: “Marlanwg is here. We have successfully accessed the internal infrastructure and retrieved a sample of your data to verify the extent of the breach”, and directed bank officials to the encrypted messaging app Session to negotiate data deletion and remediation terms. At 23:45 on 6 November the bank said its corporate website was unavailable and told customers to use its iRakyat, BRICK, QR2E and i-bizRAKYAT apps and platforms. Bank Negara Malaysia previously fined Bank Rakyat RM1 million under its Risk Management in Technology framework after a separate cybersecurity breach. On 7 November the bank said in a Facebook statement, reported by Malay Mail, that the disruption was caused by a technical problem involving a third-party service provider, that only its corporate website was affected, and that deposits, personal information and banking services were unaffected, with restoration work under way. Communications Minister Fahmi Fadzil said the same day that the incident was confined to changes to the website's appearance on a third-party-managed site, that the bank had reported the site had been hacked but the incident was limited to web defacement and takeover, and that no data theft had been detected so far; the affected server was blocked and users redirected to the i-Rakyat website, which the bank fully owns.
breaking.source_name: Pokde.Net, 6 November 2026; Siakap Keli, 6 November 2026 (translated from Malay); Malay Mail, 7 November 2026
breaking.summary: Malaysian cooperative bank Bank Rakyat's corporate website was briefly defaced on the evening of 6 November 2026 by an actor using the handle “Marlanwg”, who claimed to have accessed the bank's internal infrastructure and taken a sample of its data. The bank confirmed at 23:45 that its corporate website was unavailable and directed customers to its mobile apps and digital platforms. On 7 November the bank attributed the disruption to a technical problem involving a third-party service provider and said deposits, personal information and banking services were unaffected; the Communications Minister said the incident was limited to web defacement of a third-party-managed site with no data theft detected. The actor's claim of internal access and data theft remains unconfirmed and is now disputed by the bank.
breaking.unknown: The bank has not issued a formal statement specifically addressing the actor's claim of internal network access or data theft; it attributes the outage to a third-party technical fault and says no data was stolen. A local threat-intelligence account claims to have verified samples shared by the actor and says the data appears authentic, but this has not been independently confirmed and conflicts with the bank's and the minister's statements. Whether customer data or funds are affected, and whether the bank's wider digital services are fully restored, is unconfirmed.

breaking.bfsi_impact: Peer banks and consumer-finance firms that outsource loan guarantees should check whether their customers' data passed through the affected system, prepare for phishing and identity-fraud attempts using the leaked licence numbers and income data, and warn affected customers not to trust calls, emails or messages that cite their loan details. The leak of driver's licence numbers together with income and guarantee amounts is directly usable for impersonation and social engineering against bank customers.
breaking.headline: SMBC Consumer Finance discloses breach of up to 320,118 customers' data
breaking.known: SMBC Consumer Finance detected unauthorised access to its loan-guarantee system on 2 November and cut off access the same day; data was sent outside the company. The leaked data includes names, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, email addresses, driver's licence numbers, employer and income details, and guarantee amounts and other contract information. Images of identity documents were not included. The firm provides guarantee services to 189 financial institutions, including regional banks, credit unions and online banks; its own Promise consumer-finance service does not use the affected system and is unaffected. No secondary harm from misuse of the data had been confirmed at the time of disclosure. Since the disclosure, partner banks have confirmed their customers are among those affected: Docomo SMTB Net Bank said up to 122,635 of its customers may be affected; Hiroshima Bank said personal data of customers who applied for two of its loan products was in the leak and suspended web applications for them; Chugoku Bank said up to 25 records were affected and also suspended web applications. (Nikkei, 6 November 2026.) Ehime Bank also said its customers' data was among the leaked records and that it was still checking how many were affected (thecoauthor, 8 November 2026). The Resona group said on 6 November that 5,935 former customers across its three banks — Resona Bank (139), Kansai Mirai Bank (5,793) and Minato Bank (3) — were affected, all with card loans already closed; Bank of Yokohama also confirmed its customers were affected, without giving a number. (Pasqualepillitteri.it, 8 November 2026, citing the Resona group disclosure and Kanagawa Shimbun.) On 10 November, Fukuoka Financial Group said at an interim-results press conference that customer information of its three banks — Kumamoto Bank, Fukuoka Bank and Juhachi-Shinwa Bank — had leaked via the SMBC Consumer Finance guarantee system; the banks apologised, and the number of affected customers is still being checked. (Kumamoto Nichinichi Shimbun, 10 November 2026, translated from Japanese.)
breaking.source_name: Nikkei, 5 November 2026; TBS NEWS DIG, 5 November 2026 (translated from Japanese); Resona group disclosure via Pasqualepillitteri.it, 8 November 2026
breaking.summary: SMBC Consumer Finance, the Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group consumer-finance arm, said on 5 November 2026 that unauthorised access to its loan-guarantee system exposed personal data of up to 320,118 people, including names, birth dates, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, driver's licence numbers, employer details, income and loan guarantee amounts. The intrusion was detected on 2 November and access was cut off the same day; the guarantee system is suspended while checks continue. No misuse of the data has been confirmed so far, and images of identity documents were not included. The data covers customers of 189 partner banks, credit unions and online banks for which the firm provides loan guarantees; its own Promise consumer-finance service was not affected.
breaking.type: Named BFSI victim — major data breach
breaking.unknown: The full list of affected partner institutions is still being pinned down — Hiroshima Bank, Chugoku Bank, Docomo SMTB Net Bank, Ehime Bank and the three Fukuoka Financial Group banks have confirmed their customers are affected. Whether the intrusion exploited a specific vulnerability, and the attacker's identity, are undisclosed.

breaking.bfsi_impact: A leaked list of 227,216 corporate customer email addresses is ready-made fuel for targeted phishing and business-email compromise impersonating SMBC. Peer banks using third-party email-delivery services should check their own suppliers' exposure, and customers should treat any message citing SMBC business as suspect unless verified through known channels.
breaking.headline: Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation confirms 227,216 email addresses leaked via contractor
breaking.known: The leak came through Arara's email-delivery service 'Arara Message', used by the bank. The affected addresses are recipients of bank emails sent 1 July–31 October 2026, mainly corporate customers plus some sole proprietors. No account numbers, balances, PINs or internet-banking IDs or passwords were included. The bank was told of the unauthorised access on 28 October and received confirmation that data had leaked on 2 November. SMBC and SMBC Trust Bank also announced a new information-sharing arrangement with Japan's National Police Agency from 9 November to speed up anti-fraud cooperation.
breaking.source_name: TBS NEWS DIG, 5 November 2026 (translated from Japanese)
breaking.summary: Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation said on 5 November 2026 that unauthorised access to its email-delivery contractor Arara's 'Arara Message' service leaked 227,216 email addresses — the recipients of emails the bank sent between 1 July and 31 October, mainly corporate customers and some sole proprietors. No account numbers, balances, PINs or internet-banking IDs or passwords were included. The bank was told of the unauthorised access on 28 October and received confirmation of the leak on 2 November.
breaking.type: Named BFSI victim — third-party data breach
breaking.unknown: The cause of the unauthorised access at the contractor and the full extent of any further exposure are still being checked with the contractor. Whether any leaked addresses have been used in phishing has not been reported.

breaking.bfsi_impact: Peer banks using third-party or supplier-built mobile banking systems should review supplier security settings, account-enumeration controls and verification for non-designated transfers, and check whether any supplier system permits transfers without the customer logging in. APAC banks should watch the regulator's detailed report due 12 November.
breaking.headline: Bank SinoPac confirms hackers exploited supplier flaw in unauthorised transfers
breaking.known: At a press conference on the evening of 4 November, reported by Focus Taiwan (CNA) at 21:01 SGT, the bank said external hackers breached security settings at the supplier of its new online banking transaction system, used trial-and-error to obtain valid accounts sharing an ID-number prefix, and moved funds to a single Taipei Fubon Bank account, which was frozen. The bank said it reimbursed customers on 3 November, found no evidence of personal-data leakage, hired an independent cybersecurity team, shared threat information with peers via F-ISAC, and will seek compensation from the foreign supplier, whose system is used by no other bank in Taiwan. Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission requires a detailed major-incident report by 12 November. On 12 November Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission said at its regular press conference that the bank's detailed investigation report was due that day and had not yet been received, though the regulator expected it the same day; the FSC said it would review whether the bank carried out proper due diligence on its outsourced vendors and did not rule out fines, and it convened bank chief information security officers the same day to discuss the shift in attack patterns brought by artificial intelligence. (BigGo Finance, 12 November 2026, translated from Chinese; Mirror Daily, 12 November 2026, translated from Chinese)
breaking.source_name: Focus Taiwan (CNA), 4 November 2026; BigGo Finance, 12 November 2026 (translated from Chinese); Mirror Daily, 12 November 2026 (translated from Chinese)
breaking.summary: Taiwan's Bank SinoPac said on 4 November 2026 that external hackers exploited security settings at the supplier of its new mobile banking system, causing 427 unauthorised transfers totalling about NT$41.76 million (about US$1.27 million) on 3 November. The bank has reimbursed affected customers, the single receiving account at another bank was frozen, and the new system has been suspended.
breaking.unknown: The supplier's name, the exact flaw in its security settings, and the attackers' identity are undisclosed, and the case is under criminal investigation. Local reports of the bank's press conference put the affected customer count at 418, against the Financial Supervisory Commission / Focus Taiwan figure of 419 accounts for the same 427 transfers; the wire uses the regulator's figure and flags the one-customer discrepancy.

breaking.bfsi_impact: A named European bank victim with fraudulent transactions: peer banks should review controls on large and exchange-account withdrawals, verify transaction authorisation and suspension procedures, and watch for laundering of any linked funds through exchanges and instant-swap services. Under the EU Digital Operational Resilience Act, major ICT incidents carry a short initial reporting window, so EU-regulated peers should check their own incident-classification clocks. Third-party platform access is now a confirmed route in this case: review service-provider platforms that can reach the bank directly, not only customer-facing channels.
breaking.headline: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirms cyberattack enabling fraudulent transactions
breaking.known: The bank's own statement, reported by CoinDesk, Bloomberg and Ledger Insights on 4 November, confirms the attack and the fraudulent transactions. Blockchain investigator ZachXBT first flagged a suspected loss of more than $106 million at an unnamed EU entity on 2 November and named Arkéa on 3 November, putting the total above $133 million; Bitquery traced $108.8 million in USDC withdrawals from Kraken, Crypto.com and OKX accounts over 1–2 November, and Crypto.com said it blocked funds linked to the incident. In a further statement on the evening of 4 November, reported by AFP/Reuters and updated by CNA at 00:57 SGT on 5 November, the bank said attackers reached Arkéa directly through the platform of one of its service providers — not through Fortuneo, and not through client accounts — used the bank's own account to transfer funds to other banks, and then converted funds into cryptocurrency via specialist platforms; a portion of funds was blocked and recovery efforts are under way. The bank gave a provisional estimate of about €100 million, validated the order of magnitude of the reported $133 million (about €118 million) figure, but has not confirmed a final figure. The Paris public prosecutor's office has opened an investigation into an attack on an automated data processing system by an organised group. On 5 November the bank said nearly all operations had resumed after security checks and additional safeguards, customer funds were unaffected, and the losses were lower than the $133 million figure reported in the press and not of a nature to undermine the group's financial strength. On 6 November the president of the Crédit Mutuel confederation, Daniel Baal, told France 5 television that the bank had “already recovered part of (the missing money) today”, without saying how much; Le Télégramme put the amount taken at €118 million.
breaking.source_name: Reuters / AFP via CNA, 4-5 November 2026; Cointelegraph, 5 November 2026
breaking.summary: French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirmed on 4 November 2026 that it was the target of a cyberattack that enabled fraudulent transactions. The bank says the incident is now under control, some transactions were temporarily suspended, regulators and supervisory authorities have been notified, and clients face no financial consequences. In its evening update the bank gave a provisional estimate of about €100 million, with the final figure still being assessed.
breaking.unknown: The bank has not confirmed a final amount, the attack method, which service provider's platform was used, whether the provider itself was breached (reported by Le Figaro, not confirmed by the bank), or how much, if anything, has been recovered. The $133 million figure is the investigator's estimate, repeated in the press, not a bank-confirmed loss; the bank has validated only its order of magnitude.

entries.bfsi_impact: Indian banks and their customers should treat the alleged $3.4 million loss as unconfirmed and denied: there is no verified incident to respond to, but an allegation involving government-linked accounts is the kind of claim that fuels phishing and impersonation attempts citing YES Bank. Firms should watch for any regulator statement or further reporting, and customers should verify any message citing the alleged incident through known channels. The episode also shows how quickly an unconfirmed fraud allegation against a bank can move through the press.
entries.headline: YES Bank denies report of $3.4 million cyber fraud loss involving government accounts
entries.known: The Banker, a Financial Times Group publication, reported (title: 'India on High Alert After Alleged $3.4 Million Cyber Loss at YES Bank') that a cybersecurity incident had occurred towards the end of October 2026 involving government accounts, with a loss of about $3.4 million (Rs 32 crore). YES Bank issued a clarification on Friday 13 November 2026 rejecting the claims as factually incorrect: it said its banking systems had not been compromised, no government accounts had been affected, and it had suffered no monetary loss linked to the reported incident. The bank said it had contacted the publication to highlight what it described as factual inaccuracies and requested a retraction, warning the report could damage its reputation and create unnecessary uncertainty among customers, investors and other stakeholders. The denial was reported by Indian press on 14 November, including IANS (09:50 IST) and the Free Press Journal (10:55 IST).
entries.source_name: Free Press Journal, 14 November 2026; IANS via Lokmat Times / New Kerala, 14 November 2026
entries.summary: YES Bank has denied a report by The Banker, a Financial Times Group publication, alleging the bank suffered a cyber fraud loss of about $3.4 million (Rs 32 crore) involving government-linked accounts in an incident towards the end of October 2026. In a clarification issued on Friday 13 November, the bank said its systems were not compromised, no government accounts were affected and it suffered no financial loss, and it has asked the publication for a retraction. The allegation is unconfirmed and denied.
entries.type: Disputed cyber-fraud allegation - bank denies
entries.unknown: Whether any incident occurred at all: the allegation is unconfirmed and the bank denies it. The Banker's evidence for the alleged loss has not been published in the reporting seen, and no regulator or law-enforcement statement about the alleged incident has been reported. The Banker has not publicly responded to the retraction request in the reporting seen.

entries.bfsi_impact: South Korea's regulator now counts 16 financial firms breached in the AI-assisted hacking wave, with about 100,000 records leaked — five more firms than previously known, including a savings bank, a capital company and two virtual-asset firms. Firms with Korean exposure should treat the wave as still spreading and check the shared attacker indicators; the regulator says no account or card numbers usable for direct fraudulent payment have been confirmed leaked so far.
entries.headline: South Korea regulator counts 16 financial firms breached in AI hacking wave; about 100,000 records leaked
entries.known: South Korea's Financial Services Commission and Financial Supervisory Service said at a second emergency response meeting on 14 November 2026 that 16 financial firms across all sectors have now been confirmed breached in the recent AI-assisted hacking wave, with about 100,000 leaked records (names, contact details, resident registration numbers and email addresses) confirmed so far. Five firms were newly reported beyond those previously known: DB Savings Bank (breach on 10 November, no customer data leaked, about 100 staff records exposed), KDB Capital (attacked 10 November, 848 customers' names, resident registration numbers and birth dates), BrightPix, and virtual-asset firms Streami (operator of Gopax) and PraBank. The previously known firms include Shinhan, KB Kookmin, Hana and BNK Busan banks, Yegaram, Welcome and OK savings banks, Hyundai Capital, the National Credit Union Federation, PFCT and Modu. The regulator said firms are still checking against shared attacker IP addresses, and that no account numbers or card numbers directly usable for fraudulent payment have been confirmed leaked.
entries.source_name: Yonhap News Agency, 14 November 2026 (in Korean)
entries.summary: South Korea's financial regulator said on 14 November 2026 that 16 financial firms have now been confirmed breached in the AI-assisted hacking wave, with about 100,000 records leaked, naming five newly reported firms including DB Savings Bank, KDB Capital and the Gopax operator Streami. No account or card numbers usable for direct fraudulent payment have been confirmed leaked.
entries.type: Sector regulator update — AI-driven hacking wave
entries.unknown: Whether further firms will be confirmed as checks against the shared attacker indicators continue, and the full breakdown of the roughly 100,000 leaked records by firm.

entries.bfsi_impact: If genuine, a ransomware listing naming a US auto lender and a major private-equity firm would extend the Payoutsking campaign into financial services; treat as unverified until either firm or a primary source confirms it, and watch for a published data sample or a company statement.
entries.headline: Payoutsking lists iLending and J.C. Flowers & Co. as ransomware victims; claim unverified
entries.known: The Payoutsking ransomware group listed iLending and J.C. Flowers & Co. on its dark-web leak site on 12 November 2026, according to ransomware-tracking records. Both organisations operate in the financial services sector in the United States. No ransom demand, data sample or victim statement has been reported, and the specific data said to have been stolen has not been independently verified.
entries.source_name: Cyber Threat Intelligence (ransomware-tracking record), updated 14 November 2026
entries.summary: The Payoutsking ransomware group listed US financial services firms iLending and J.C. Flowers & Co. as victims on its leak site on 12 November 2026. Neither firm has confirmed a breach and the claim is unverified.
entries.type: Unverified ransomware claim — financial services firms
entries.unknown: Whether Payoutsking actually breached either firm, what data if any it holds, and whether any ransom demand was made.

entries.bfsi_impact: If genuine, a breach at the operator of Jamaica's national debit-card and clearing networks would be a sector-critical incident; Jamaican banks and their customers should watch for a JETS or Bank of Jamaica statement and for any published data, and treat the claim as unverified until then. Even as an unverified claim, it follows JETS' own admission of an intrusion into its administrative systems last month.
entries.headline: INC Ransom claims Jamaica's JETS payment network operator; claim unverified
entries.known: INC Ransom has listed Jamaica Electronic Transfer Services (JETS) on its dark-web leak site and claims to have taken data from the company, according to a listing picked up on 13 November by Ransomware.live; the listing puts the estimated attack date at 21 October. JETS operates Jamaica's Multi-Link debit-card network and its Automated Clearing House payment network. Last month JETS admitted hackers had gained access to a limited part of its internal administrative systems, and said the Multi-Link and ACH networks themselves were not compromised and are operating normally. Jamaica's technology minister has asked JETS and the Bank of Jamaica for a full report, including whether any ransom demand was received. Customers have been urged to monitor bank accounts and report suspicious transactions.
entries.source_name: Nationwide News Network (Jamaica), 13 November 2026
entries.summary: The INC Ransom ransomware group has listed Jamaica Electronic Transfer Services (JETS) - operator of the country's Multi-Link debit-card and ACH payment networks - on its dark-web leak site, claiming to have taken data. JETS said last month that hackers had accessed a limited part of its internal administrative systems; the group says the payment networks were not compromised and are operating normally. The claim is unverified.
entries.type: Unverified ransomware claim - payment network operator
entries.unknown: Whether INC Ransom actually took data, what data if any it holds, and whether any ransom demand was made. Nationwide News says it has not been able to verify the group's claims.

entries.bfsi_impact: Directly relevant to lenders and their banking partners: payout APIs are a live fraud route, and the Rs 1 test-transfer pattern is an early warning. Firms should check for exposed test environments, credentials in source code and long-lived partner tokens, enforce short-lived credentials, transaction limits and independent maker-checker approvals, and reconcile every payout against an approved loan transaction in real time. The CERT-In 'Crafty Falcon' advisory of 4 November already covers this campaign; this reporting adds named victims, figures and the multi-state scope.
entries.headline: Indian NBFC payout APIs exploited in 'Crafty Falcon' fraud wave; three Telangana lenders lose about Rs 18 crore
entries.known: Cybercriminals exploited the payout APIs of Indian non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), with three Telangana lenders reporting 304 fraudulent transactions between 19 October and 6 November 2026. VIVIFI Indian Finance detected 183 fraudulent transactions worth Rs 3.34 crore within 88 minutes on 19 October; Spandana Sphoorthy Financial reported 82 transactions amounting to Rs 7.8 crore on 1 November; Keerthana Finserv detected 39 transactions worth around Rs 7 crore on 6 November. Similar attacks were reported in six other states and Union territories (Karnataka, Maharashtra, Delhi, Chandigarh, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry). Siphoned funds were diverted through 50-60 bank accounts in each case before being transferred to gaming and betting applications, including Dafabet, 1xBet, WinZO, Betway, My11Circle and Bet365. IP addresses associated with the attacks were traced to Turkey, Cambodia, China, Japan, Malaysia and Hong Kong, and recipient accounts in Bengaluru surfaced in all three Telangana cases, although no common accounts or IP addresses were found across the incidents. The Telangana Cyber Security Bureau attributes the exposure to exposed testing environments, outdated APIs, credentials embedded in source code and partner tokens that remain valid for too long. CERT-In's advisory of 4 November flagged an AI-assisted campaign designated 'CRAFTY FALCON' involving exposed testing systems, shared credentials, Rs 1 test transfers and unauthorised payouts, and repeat attacks were reported where remediation was incomplete. Arrests in the Hero FinCorp investigation (five people) concern alleged receipt and conversion of proceeds into USDT and do not establish who carried out the original intrusions.
entries.source_name: The Times of India, 13 November 2026
entries.summary: Cybercriminals exploited the payout APIs of Indian non-banking financial companies, with three Telangana lenders reporting 304 fraudulent transactions between 19 October and 6 November 2026: VIVIFI Indian Finance (183 transactions, Rs 3.34 crore, 19 October), Spandana Sphoorthy Financial (82 transactions, Rs 7.8 crore, 1 November) and Keerthana Finserv (39 transactions, around Rs 7 crore, 6 November). Similar attacks were reported in six other states and Union territories, with cumulative losses across India estimated in the hundreds of crores of rupees. The reporting ties the attacks to the 'Crafty Falcon' campaign CERT-In flagged on 4 November.
entries.type: Lender payment fraud - API exploitation
entries.unknown: Whether AI was used in the Telangana incidents remains under examination. The national loss figure ('hundreds of crores of rupees') is an estimate, not a confirmed total. The attackers behind the Telangana incidents have not been identified; traced IP addresses in six countries do not by themselves establish the attackers' location. How transfers succeeded despite measures intended to block foreign VPN access is still being examined.

entries.bfsi_impact: Brazil's federal treasury runs the government's cash and payments, so the exposed Pix keys and CPFs are direct fraud material for impersonating the Treasury and federal payment recipients. Firms with Brazilian exposure should warn customers and staff about contact purporting to come from the Tesouro Nacional, and treat the leaked names, CPFs and Pix keys as active impersonation material. No payment system was compromised, so there is no direct transfer risk, but Pix-key exposure raises the credibility of payment-fraud approaches.
entries.headline: Brazil's National Treasury confirms data leak; 30,000 registrations and 4,000 Pix keys exposed
entries.known: Brazil's National Treasury (Secretaria do Tesouro Nacional, STN) confirmed on the evening of 12 November 2026 that unauthorised access detected on 4 November exposed personal data in two databases. The larger is the e-Servicos portal, where the public requests and tracks Treasury services: names, CPFs (Brazilian tax IDs) and email addresses of about 30,000 registrations. The smaller is an internal analytical database used to study federal payments already made: about 4,000 Pix keys of payment recipients, with data on those payments. The Treasury said there was no financial impact and no core payment system was compromised, and warned the exposed data could be used to make fraud attempts more convincing. It notified the data-protection authority (ANPD) and the government incident-response centre (CTIR Gov), and a technical investigation is under way to establish the origin and extent of the access. Affected people can contact the Ministry of Finance data officer via the Fala.BR platform.
entries.source_name: Agencia Brasil, 12 November 2026; Olhar Digital, 12 November 2026 (translated from Portuguese)
entries.summary: Brazil's National Treasury confirmed on 12 November 2026 that unauthorised access detected on 4 November exposed the registration data of about 30,000 users of its e-Servicos portal - names, CPFs (tax IDs) and email addresses - plus about 4,000 Pix keys of federal payment recipients from an internal analytical database. The Treasury said there was no financial impact and no core payment system was compromised, and it notified the ANPD and CTIR Gov.
entries.type: Government finance - data breach
entries.unknown: The attacker and the entry route have not been disclosed. Whether the exposed payment data includes amounts, dates or recipient names beyond the Pix keys has not been specified. No misuse of the exposed data has been reported.

entries.bfsi_impact: Directly relevant to crypto exchanges, digital-asset firms and their staff, and to any financial firm whose people join video calls with external contacts: deepfake video-call social engineering is a live fraud vector, and reuse of a victim's recorded video against their contacts makes the approach hard to spot. Firms should brief staff to verify meeting links and unexpected video-call invitations out of band, and treat any request to install software during a call as a red flag. The separate $1.2 billion Binance seizure is a recovery action, not a new loss.
entries.headline: FBI says North Korean 'FaceStealer' campaign stole over $400 million in crypto via fake video calls
entries.known: The FBI and the US Department of Justice said on 12 November 2026 that North Korean hackers tracked as Sapphire Sleet (also UNC1069, Stardust Chollima, BlueNoroff, APT38) stole more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over 18 months through a social-engineering scheme the FBI calls FaceStealer. Targets in the cryptocurrency and Web3 sectors, and open-source developers, are lured to video meetings on imposter versions of Zoom, Microsoft Teams and Google Meet, invited from accounts stolen from earlier victims. The target's webcam is secretly recorded while a pre-recorded video of a trusted contact plays, and victims are tricked into installing crypto-stealing malware disguised as an audio fix; the recorded video is then reused against the next victim. The FBI said it seized more than 900 victim webcam videos under a federal warrant and disrupted the cloud infrastructure behind the scheme under a court order, and published a technical report with warning signs. Parts of the activity overlap a campaign Kaspersky documented as GhostCall in October 2025 and a JUMPSEC report from July 2026 on the fake-meeting phishing kit. In the same announcement, the Justice Department said a court authorised the seizure or restraint of more than $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen in the October 2026 Binance hack, attributed to a different North Korean cluster, TraderTraitor.
entries.source_name: Reuters, 12 November 2026; The Hacker News, 12 November 2026
entries.summary: The FBI said on 12 November 2026 that North Korean hackers tracked as Sapphire Sleet (UNC1069) stole more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over 18 months through a social-engineering scheme the FBI calls FaceStealer, using fake Zoom, Teams and Google Meet calls to record victims' webcams and lure their contacts. The FBI said it seized more than 900 victim webcam videos and disrupted the cloud infrastructure behind the scheme. In the same announcement, the Justice Department said a court authorised the seizure or restraint of more than $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency stolen in the October Binance hack, attributed to a different North Korean cluster, TraderTraitor.
entries.type: FBI advisory - DPRK crypto-theft campaign
entries.unknown: The FBI has not named individual victims or said how many of the 900-plus recorded people had funds stolen. Whether any bank or regulated financial institution was directly targeted has not been stated. The FBI's technical report (IC3 FLASH advisory CSA-261112, dated 11 November) carries the indicators and warning signs.

entries.bfsi_impact: A small Canadian advisory and brokerage firm named in an unverified extortion claim: peers should watch for a confirmation or denial from the firm and for any data sample, and treat the claim as unconfirmed until then.
entries.headline: PixelLeaks claims Canadian advisory firm Four Points Financial as breach victim; claim unverified
entries.known: Breachsense, which monitors ransomware leak sites and dark-web sources, recorded on 13 November 2026 that the actor PixelLeaks claims Four Points Financial Solutions Inc. as a breach victim; the leak size is unknown and no data sample is published. Four Points Financial Solutions Inc. is an independent financial advisory and brokerage firm based in Canada, offering wealth planning and access to insurance, investment, banking and trust products. Breachsense states the claim has not been verified.
entries.source_name: Breachsense, 13 November 2026
entries.summary: Breachsense recorded on 13 November 2026 that the actor PixelLeaks claims Four Points Financial Solutions Inc., a Canadian independent financial advisory and brokerage firm, as a breach victim; the claim is unverified and no leak size or data sample is published.
entries.type: Ransomware/extortion claim — unverified
entries.unknown: Whether any breach occurred, what data (if any) was taken, and the firm's response are all unknown; no data sample has been published and no time of day was given for the claim's discovery.

entries.bfsi_impact: Banking and finance is one of the critical information infrastructure sectors CSA says it has briefed; Singapore banks and financial firms should treat the tripling of reported incidents as a prompt to check exposed and unpatched systems, the four gaps CSA lists, and to report incidents to SingCERT. The advisory is general, not BFSI-specific, and names no financial victim.
entries.headline: CSA Singapore issues advisory as reported cyber incidents triple since September
entries.known: Singapore's Cyber Security Agency issued Advisory AD-2026-017 on 13 November 2026 urging all organisations to strengthen cyber defences now. CSA said the average monthly number of reported cyber incidents since September is three times the January-August average, and at least 12 incidents involving Singapore organisations or their service providers were reported between 24 October and 13 November. CSA said the incidents appear to reflect a broader global trend of opportunistic attacks rather than coordinated campaigns targeting Singapore, with attackers scanning for weak systems and using AI to find and exploit weaknesses faster. The Personal Data Protection Commission said separately on 13 November that the data breaches it observed arose from attacks exploiting common vulnerabilities in IT systems. CSA said it has briefed all critical information infrastructure sectors, including banking and finance, and is working closely with CII owners. The latest case reported on 13 November involved local clothing label Our Second Nature, whose customer details were exposed in a breach discovered a week earlier.
entries.source_name: Channel NewsAsia, 13 November 2026; The Straits Times, 13 November 2026
entries.summary: Singapore's Cyber Security Agency issued Advisory AD-2026-017 on 13 November 2026 urging all organisations to strengthen cyber defences, saying the average monthly number of reported cyber incidents since September is three times the January-August average; CSA has briefed critical information infrastructure sectors, including banking and finance.
entries.type: Government advisory — sector alert (general; CII sectors briefed)
entries.unknown: No BFSI-specific directive or victim is named in the advisory, and CSA has not published a breakdown of how many of the reported incidents involved financial firms.

entries.bfsi_impact: A small but confirmed leak at a Korean virtual-asset exchange, in the same week as the wider Korean financial-sector incident wave: 40 customers is a limited exposure, but affected customers should be warned about phishing using their exchange-account details.
entries.headline: Flybit crypto exchange confirms personal data of 40 customers leaked
entries.known: Korea Digital Exchange, operator of the Flybit virtual-asset exchange, suffered a leak of personal data of 40 customers through unauthorised external access on 1 November 2026. The disclosure was reported on 13 November 2026 alongside the KB Capital breach.
entries.source_name: NoCut News, 13 November 2026 (translated from Korean)
entries.summary: Korea Digital Exchange, operator of the Flybit virtual-asset exchange, suffered a leak of personal data of 40 customers through unauthorised external access on 1 November 2026, disclosed on 13 November.
entries.type: Named BFSI victim — data breach
entries.unknown: The entry route, the exact data items exposed and whether any customer funds were affected have not been disclosed.

entries.bfsi_impact: A third confirmed breach in South Korea's capital-finance sector in two months, extending the financial-sector incident wave already tracked in the FSI breaking item: firms with Korean exposure should treat the leaked names, phone numbers and vehicle details as phishing and voice-phishing material, and watch for the expected Financial Supervisory Service on-site inspection. Direct account-takeover risk is limited — the breached system handles vehicle leases, not financial transactions, and only 20 customers were affected — but staff and partner account details could support impersonation and business-email compromise.
entries.headline: KB Capital confirms breach; personal data of 1,811 people leaked
entries.known: KB Capital, the capital-finance arm of South Korea's KB Financial Group, said on 13 November 2026 that a malicious attack detected on 10 November exposed personal data of 1,811 people — 20 customers and about 1,791 partner-company employees and staff — from its vehicle lease asset management system. The company detected the breach after repeated abnormal information lookups from a domestic IP address, halted the affected systems and servers, blocked the external access route and reported the incident to the Financial Supervisory Service the same day. It posted a notice on its website with a self-check service for affected individuals and promised full compensation for any loss. Exposed customer data: names, dates of birth, mobile phone numbers, addresses and vehicle registration numbers. Exposed staff and partner data: user accounts, names, mobile and landline numbers, department names, company names and job titles. This is the third confirmed breach in Korea's capital-finance sector after Hyundai Capital (146 mortgage loan agents, September) and KDB Capital (848 customers, October). The FSS is expected to carry out an on-site inspection.
entries.source_name: Seoul Economic Daily, 13 November 2026; NoCut News, 13 November 2026 (translated from Korean)
entries.summary: KB Capital, the capital-finance arm of South Korea's KB Financial Group, said on 13 November 2026 that a malicious attack detected on 10 November exposed personal data of 1,811 people — 20 customers and about 1,791 partner-company employees and staff — from its vehicle lease asset management system. Names, birth dates, mobile numbers, addresses and vehicle registration numbers were exposed for customers; user accounts, names, phone numbers, departments, company names and job titles for staff and partners. The system is unrelated to financial transactions.
entries.type: Named BFSI victim — data breach
entries.unknown: The attacker and the entry route have not been disclosed. Whether this incident is linked to the 9 November Financial Security Institute breach is unconfirmed — both involved domestic IP addresses and the FSI breach was detected a day earlier, but no link has been established. The company notes the 1,811 figure may include duplicates and could change as the investigation continues.

entries.bfsi_impact: MSPs are the route into small banks' and financial firms' endpoints, so firms should ask their providers whether they run ScreenConnect with the RMM+ extension, hunt for RelayTrap, the TrapWatch task and the rogue client IDs, and check RMM+ versions 1.0.31/1.0.32. The correction matters: the technician-trap spread is designed behaviour, not observed — the immediate risk is the rogue clients already deployed, not a self-propagating worm.
entries.headline: SCKit worm toolkit named in ScreenConnect MSP attacks; RMM+ blank-key flaw is the entry route
entries.known: Huntress and Blackpoint Cyber have named the toolkit behind this week's ScreenConnect MSP attacks SCKit: 16 scripts and components that install a rogue ScreenConnect client plus a RelayTrap component designed to steal a technician's session cookie when the technician connects to an infected device. RelayTrap reads the technician's .aspxauth session cookie from browser cookie databases with a SQLite tool and tries to replay it against the panel, then uploads a payload to the panel's Shared Toolbox to reach every session the technician can access; it installs a scheduled task named TrapWatch running as SYSTEM. The entry route is the third-party RMM+ extension versions 1.0.31/1.0.32, which accepted a blank access key when none was configured, bypassing ScreenConnect accounts, roles and multi-factor authentication; RMM+ commands appeared in logs with no corresponding logins. A new CVE, CVE-2026-127063 (9.3), covers the RMM+ extension's static API secret — its wording differs from Huntress's blank-key account, so treat it as the same weakness pending vendor confirmation. Huntress is explicit that the technician-trap spread has not been observed to succeed: the console-takeover attempt failed in every recovered host log checked. Blackpoint links the RelayTrap behaviour to CVE-2026-84869 as a claim only, and reproduced the toolkit's attempted exploit against a current ScreenConnect client and found the existing patch prevented execution. ConnectWise says it found no evidence of compromise of its infrastructure or a vulnerability in ScreenConnect itself. New indicator: cdn007-digitaldownloads.com. At least 288 endpoints across 48 organisations were hit within about 90 minutes.
entries.source_name: Huntress, 12 November 2026; BleepingComputer, 12 November 2026; Blackpoint Cyber
entries.summary: Huntress and Blackpoint Cyber have named the toolkit behind this week's ScreenConnect MSP attacks SCKit: a 16-component toolkit that installs a rogue ScreenConnect client and a RelayTrap component designed to steal a technician's session cookie when they connect to an infected device. The entry route is the third-party RMM+ extension, which accepted a blank access key in versions 1.0.31/1.0.32, bypassing ScreenConnect accounts, roles and multi-factor authentication (new CVE-2026-127063). Huntress is explicit that the technician-trap spread has not been observed to succeed, and Blackpoint found the existing patch blocks the toolkit's attempted CVE-2026-84869 exploit on current clients.
entries.type: Active campaign — MSP remote-access abuse (update)
entries.unknown: Whether the technician-trap spread can succeed in practice; the full count of compromised MSPs; whether ransomware or other payloads will be deployed through the rogue clients already installed.

entries.bfsi_impact: Financial firms running CI/CD on GitHub should audit GitHub Actions secrets, cloud credentials, SSH keys and AI service keys for wfx-loot exposure, hunt for wfx-docs pull requests and gaps in Actions run numbers, check pinned versions of the affected packages, and rotate anything that may have been exfiltrated: stolen cloud credentials can be turned into persistent access, and the payload reached public package registries.
entries.headline: wfx-loot campaign uses 4,837 hijacked GitHub accounts to steal CI and cloud credentials from 1,800+ repositories
entries.known: From 10 November 12:45 UTC, an attacker used stolen GitHub credentials (personal access tokens, bot tokens, Fly.io GitHub App tokens) from 4,837 compromised accounts to open probe pull requests — branch wfx-docs, titled 'docs: dependency audit notes' — in 61,764 repositories, testing for write access. Where access allowed, the attacker injected a roughly 1,500-line payload that steals GitHub Actions secrets, cloud credentials (AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, including via instance metadata on self-hosted runners), SSH keys, shell history and AI service keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cursor, Copilot). At least 1,806-1,835 repositories ran the payload with credentials exfiltrated; SafeDep counts 8,093 commits pushed on public default branches. The attacker deletes workflow runs within a minute, so gaps in run numbers are the tell. The payload leaked into Packagist digitalelvis/neuronai-studio 3.14.3 and Go modules (github.com/onuragtas/docker-env v1.0.278/280, gocurl, redock), plus npm pdf-html5-page-flip 2.0.1/2.0.2 (removed 12 November; GHSA-j3hx-5mxx-43qh). Some compromised accounts belonged to Fortune 100 organisations, the US General Services Administration, the French government, Nextcloud and WebdriverIO; about 50 accounts have publishing rights on npm, PyPI, Go, crates and Packagist. The exfiltration IP 193.32.204.199 is the same as the October GhostAction wave, and wfx-loot was injected into GhostAction workflow files in over 100 repositories, but Aikido assesses the two waves are likely different actors. GitHub itself was not exploited; valid stolen tokens were used. The campaign was still active on 12 November, with 4,100+ new probes on 12 November alone. Confirmed by two independent analyses (Aikido and SafeDep).
entries.source_name: Aikido Security, 12 November 2026; BleepingComputer, 12 November 2026
entries.summary: From 10 November, an attacker used stolen GitHub credentials from 4,837 compromised accounts to open probe pull requests in 61,764 repositories and inject a CI secret stealer that harvests GitHub Actions secrets, cloud credentials, SSH keys and AI service keys. At least 1,806-1,835 repositories ran the payload with credentials exfiltrated. Some compromised accounts belonged to Fortune 100 organisations and government bodies; the payload leaked into Packagist, Go and npm packages. GitHub itself was not exploited — valid stolen tokens were used — and the campaign was still active on 12 November.
entries.type: Active campaign — CI/CD credential theft
entries.unknown: The attacker's identity; the full set of affected repositories and whether any financial firm's CI was among them; whether stolen cloud credentials have been used beyond the campaign.

entries.bfsi_impact: Banks running Check Point gateways with exposed Mobile Access portals should apply the November Jumbo Hotfix immediately: the chain gives unauthenticated remote code execution followed by root, with persistence and lateral movement to virtualisation hosts. Unpatched gateways exposed to the internet should be treated as potentially compromised and hunted for the webshell and TSGA indicators.
entries.headline: Check Point confirms PHP2Shell actively exploited on its gateways, chained with new privilege-escalation flaw
entries.known: Check Point Research said on 12 November 2026 that from 30 October an attacker scanned and exploited organisations running unpatched Check Point Security Gateways through Mobile Access portals, using PHP2Shell as initial access and then CVE-2026-123039, a local privilege-escalation flaw in the DynamicCLI interface, to escalate from the portal service account to root. The attacker then deployed PHP webshells and the persistent TSGA backdoor with its embedded TSProxy networking component, and in the investigated intrusion pivoted to a VMware ESXi host and deployed the destroy_v6 wiper, leaving politically themed DREAM_ANNEXATION.txt notes. The first wave on 30 October targeted Israeli organisations and included destructive activity against some; a broader second wave on 2 November targeted organisations across multiple countries and sectors with no evidence of destructive activity and no clear sector preference. Fixes were available from 23 October. TSGA and TSProxy are modified variants of PhiliKit, previously linked by ESET to China-nexus group UNC5221, but Check Point says the evidence does not allow a high-confidence assessment of the operation's true nature, and several scenarios — including a false flag — remain plausible.
entries.source_name: Check Point Research, 12 November 2026
entries.summary: Check Point has confirmed that PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618/109619) was actively exploited against unpatched Check Point Security Gateways from 30 October, chained with a new local privilege-escalation flaw, CVE-2026-123039, to reach root. The first wave hit Israeli organisations, some with destructive wiper activity; a broader second wave on 2 November hit organisations in multiple countries and sectors.
entries.type: Active exploitation — vendor-confirmed
entries.unknown: How many organisations were compromised in total, whether any BFSI organisation was among them, and the true identity and motive of the attacker. Check Point has not named affected customers.

entries.bfsi_impact: Alleged unauthorised transfers from customer accounts at Sudan's largest bank, via its main mobile banking app; if confirmed, other banks in the region using similar mobile banking platforms should review app security and account-freeze procedures. Until the bank or a regulator responds, treat this as an unconfirmed allegation, not a confirmed breach.
entries.headline: Customers allege millions stolen from Bank of Khartoum accounts via Bankak app; bank has not responded
entries.known: Radio Dabanga reported on 12 November 2026 that more than 50 traders and customers in West Kordofan say money was stolen from their Bank of Khartoum accounts, allegedly through the bank's Bankak mobile banking app. The Dar Hamar Emergency Rooms documented the cases, with individual losses reported at SDG 18 million to SDG 45 million per person; one customer reported SDG 12 million stolen on 14 October without receiving suspicious messages or opening links. Affected people are preparing collective legal action, accusing the bank of failing to safeguard deposits and to freeze compromised accounts, and have formally raised the matter with the Bank of Khartoum, the Central Bank of Sudan and the Public Prosecution. The Bank of Khartoum has not responded to requests for comment.
entries.source_name: Radio Dabanga via wansom.ai, 12 November 2026
entries.summary: More than 50 traders and customers in Sudan's West Kordofan region say millions of Sudanese pounds were stolen from their Bank of Khartoum accounts through the Bankak mobile banking app. The cases were documented by the Dar Hamar Emergency Rooms; the bank has not responded to requests for comment.
entries.type: Alleged mobile-banking fraud — named BFSI victim
entries.unknown: Whether the app or the bank's systems were actually breached, how the transfers were made, and the true total stolen: figures vary between reports, and no technical evidence has been published. The bank has not confirmed any incident.

entries.bfsi_impact: NetScaler Gateway is a common remote-access front door for banks, and the Console bypass needs only network access to the Console IP: BFSI teams should patch ADC, Gateway and Console promptly and restrict Console access to trusted networks. No exploitation has been reported, so this is a patch-now item rather than an active incident.
entries.headline: Citrix patches 12 NetScaler flaws, including unauthenticated Console bypass rated 9.4
entries.known: Citrix released security updates on 12 November 2026 for NetScaler ADC, NetScaler Gateway and NetScaler Console, fixing 12 flaws. The most severe are CVE-2026-120869 (CVSS 9.4), an unauthenticated authentication bypass in NetScaler Console that needs only network access to the Console, and CVE-2026-120868 (CVSS 9.3), a memory overflow in packet processing affecting ADC and Gateway deployments. Citrix states it is not aware of any exploits and released no indicators of compromise.
entries.source_name: Citrix, 12 November 2026; The Hacker News, 12 November 2026
entries.summary: Citrix has patched 12 NetScaler flaws, including CVE-2026-120869, an unauthenticated NetScaler Console authentication bypass rated 9.4, and CVE-2026-120868, a packet-processing memory overflow rated 9.3. Citrix says it is not aware of any exploitation.
entries.type: Critical vulnerability — patch available
entries.unknown: Whether any of the flaws is being exploited in the wild; no exploitation evidence or proof of concept has been reported.

entries.summary: INC Ransom has listed Louisiana wealth manager Game Changer Wealth on its leak site. No data has been published and the claim is unverified.
