entries.bfsi_impact: A coordinated campaign against small US lenders through a shared managed-service-provider weakness, with confirmed Social Security number exposure at one bank: small banks and credit unions should check their MSP's remote-administration software and confirm their own exposure, and treat the four unconfirmed claims as unverified until the banks respond.
entries.headline: Sawyer Savings Bank confirms breach of 16,069 people in Storm-1175 campaign against US lenders
entries.known: TMC Insight reported on 12 November 2026 that a ransomware operation linked to Storm-1175 has claimed attacks against five US banks plus Insight Credit Union. Sawyer Savings Bank disclosed a breach affecting a reported 16,069 people, exposing names and Social Security numbers, and attributed the compromise to its managed-service provider; the bank identified the incident on 3 August 2026, completed its file review on 21 September, and sent notification letters dated 9 October, with filings to the Massachusetts, New Hampshire and Vermont attorneys general. Insight Credit Union also confirmed a breach. The group is suspected of exploiting a flaw in software used by managed-service providers to administer client systems, though the reporting does not establish that every claimed victim was compromised through the same route. This item was published at 17:48 SGT on 12 November and missed by the 20:00 wire check.
entries.source_name: TMC Insight (based on American Banker reporting), 12 November 2026
entries.summary: Sawyer Savings Bank has confirmed a breach affecting a reported 16,069 people, exposing names and Social Security numbers, after a ransomware operation linked to Storm-1175 claimed attacks on six US lenders. Insight Credit Union, already on the wire, also confirmed a breach; the other four claimed banks have not confirmed incidents.
entries.type: Confirmed breach — named BFSI victim
entries.unknown: Whether the other four claimed banks were actually breached, the full scope of the Storm-1175 campaign, and whether the MSP flaw is the common entry route for all victims. The 16,069 total comes from press reporting; the bank's state filings list only per-state counts, so the total is not confirmed by the filings themselves.

entries.bfsi_impact: A third Japanese bank has now confirmed a shareholder email leak through the same Arara mail-delivery system, suggesting a shared supplier incident rather than isolated cases: banks using Arara or similar outsourced mailing services should check whether their shareholder or customer mailings were exposed, and warn recipients about impersonation mail. The leaked data is limited to email addresses, so the direct harm is phishing risk rather than account takeover.
entries.headline: Hyakujushi Bank says 1,500 shareholder email addresses leaked via contractor's mail system
entries.known: Hyakujushi Bank (Takamatsu) said on 12 November 2026 that unauthorised access to a mail-delivery service used by a company it had commissioned leaked the email addresses of 1,500 shareholders. The commissioned company used the Arara mail-delivery system to send electronic-gift winning notices in July 2026, and the 1,500 addresses in that mailing leaked. Shareholder numbers and other attributes and the mail text were not included, the bank said. No misuse of the leaked addresses had been confirmed, and the bank warned shareholders to beware of suspicious mail purporting to come from the bank or related parties. This is the same Arara system involved in the MUFG and Nomura Holdings shareholder email leaks reported on 11 November.
entries.source_name: KSB Setouchi Broadcasting via Yahoo News Japan, 12 November 2026 (translated from Japanese)
entries.summary: Hyakujushi Bank said on 12 November that 1,500 shareholder email addresses leaked after unauthorised access to a mail-delivery service used by a contractor — the same Arara system behind the MUFG and Nomura leaks. No misuse has been confirmed.
entries.type: Named BFSI victim — confirmed data leak
entries.unknown: How the Arara system was accessed, and whether other Arara customers beyond MUFG, Nomura and Hyakujushi are affected.

entries.bfsi_impact: A telecom supplier's open database exposed bank account identifiers, balances and live one-time passwords — material that could support account takeover and fraud: banks using third-party SMS providers should confirm their provider's data handling and whether their customers' messages were in the exposed set, and consider the exposed one-time codes compromised.
entries.headline: Open database at CSC Telecom exposed 125 million SMS, including Swedbank account details and one-time codes
entries.known: Cybernews reported on 11 November 2026 that an open ClickHouse database belonging to Latvian telecom company CSC Telecom exposed more than 125 million SMS messages, covering October 2022 to September 2026, including messages for Swedbank and SEB customers in Latvia. The exposed data included Swedbank IBANs, transaction amounts and account balances, as well as login codes and one-time passwords, some visible in real time. Swedbank has suspended the provider and is investigating; SEB said only pension-fund marketing messages were involved. Latvia's CERT.LV is investigating. No evidence of malicious access to the database has been reported. This item was published before the 20:00 wire check on 12 November and missed by it.
entries.source_name: LSM English, 12 November 2026; Cybernews, 11 November 2026
entries.summary: An open ClickHouse database at Latvian telecom provider CSC Telecom exposed more than 125 million SMS messages sent between October 2022 and September 2026, including Swedbank customers' IBANs, transaction amounts and balances, and login codes and one-time passwords in real time. Swedbank has suspended the provider and is investigating; no evidence of malicious access has been reported.
entries.type: Third-party exposure — bank customer data
entries.unknown: Whether anyone accessed or copied the exposed data before it was secured, and the full range of banks and customers affected beyond Swedbank and SEB.

entries.bfsi_impact: If genuine, a breach at a Hong Kong-listed securities firm holding SFC licences across dealing, advising and asset management would put client, trading and counterparty data at risk, including ISDA documentation with 20 global banks; firms with Shenwan Hongyuan exposure should watch for a company statement and for any published data, and treat the claim as unverified until then.
entries.headline: INC Ransom lists Hong Kong brokerage Shenwan Hongyuan on leak site; claim unverified
entries.known: The INC Ransom (Incransom) ransomware group has listed Shenwan Hongyuan (H.K.) Limited on its dark-web leak site, according to Dark Web Intelligence, reported on 12 November 2026; no precise listing time was published, so the wire uses a midday timestamp. Shenwan Hongyuan (H.K.) is the Hong Kong-listed brokerage subsidiary of China's Shenwan Hongyuan Group (stock code 0218), regulated by Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission. The company disclosed on 23 October 2026 that it had received a suspected extortion message claiming information had been obtained, reported the matter to the Hong Kong Police, and said trading, settlement and core systems were operating normally with no loss of customer assets or funds. The leak-site post, as summarised by ransomware.live, claims about 21 million files totalling 9.97 TB were exfiltrated, including trading positions, derivative portfolios, ISDA agreements with 20 global banks and employee records — but no sample, ransom deadline or technical evidence has been published, and none of the claimed figures has been independently verified.
entries.source_name: Undercode News (citing Dark Web Intelligence), 12 November 2026; ransomware.live, 12 November 2026
entries.summary: INC Ransom has listed Hong Kong-listed brokerage Shenwan Hongyuan (H.K.) on its leak site, following the firm's 23 October disclosure of a suspected extortion attempt. The group's claimed haul of about 21 million files is unverified: no sample or evidence has been published, and the firm has said trading and customer assets are unaffected.
entries.type: Unverified ransomware claim — named BFSI victim
entries.unknown: Whether INC Ransom actually breached the firm's systems, what data if any was taken, whether the group behind the October extortion message is INC Ransom, and whether the firm will issue a further disclosure.

entries.bfsi_impact: A small but confirmed leak of identity documents at a Japanese bank: the exposed residence-card images could support identity fraud or account-opening scams, so affected holders should be warned, and banks should note that peripheral customer-service sites — not core banking — were the entry point. No financial fraud has been confirmed.
entries.headline: Seven Bank discloses unauthorised access; up to 150 residence-card records may have leaked
entries.known: Seven Bank (TSE Prime 8410) said on 11 November 2026 that its residence-card submission site for foreign-resident account holders and its account-cancellation site had suffered unauthorised access by a third party. The bank found traces of the access on 9 November, immediately stopped both systems and blocked access from the attacker. Up to about 150 residence-card face-image records held on the submission site may have leaked; the cards show the holder's name, date of birth, nationality or region, address and residence status. The affected people are those who received a notice of incomplete documents through the site, or who used it between 16 October and 9 November. No fraudulent transfers, unauthorised account cancellations, data tampering or misuse of the information had been confirmed, and ATM transactions, internet banking and debit services are unaffected. The cause and full scope are still under investigation, and the two sites remain suspended.
entries.source_name: Seven Bank notice, 11 November 2026 (translated from Japanese), reported by Act, 12 November 2026
entries.summary: Seven Bank said on 11 November that unauthorised access to its residence-card submission and account-cancellation sites may have leaked up to about 150 residence-card records. The bank found the access on 9 November and suspended both sites; no fraudulent transactions have been confirmed and core banking services are unaffected.
entries.type: Named BFSI victim — confirmed unauthorised access
entries.unknown: The entry route and whether any of the up-to-150 records were actually taken; the investigation is ongoing.

entries.bfsi_impact: Banks and financial firms that rely on MSPs for IT support should ask their providers whether they use ScreenConnect, check Run Command history for rogue client deployments, and treat any MSP session as untrusted until the provider confirms its environment is clean: the campaign shows an MSP compromise can reach straight into customer networks, and the possible reverse-pivot means a single infected customer device could expose the MSP's whole client base. Firms running ScreenConnect themselves should review account activity, revoke active sessions, reset credentials from a trusted device, verify multi-factor authentication, and hunt for the published indicators.
entries.headline: Active ScreenConnect campaign compromises MSPs and plants rogue remote access on customer devices
entries.known: Cybersecurity firm Huntress discovered on 11 November 2026 an active campaign, which began around 17:47 UTC (01:47 SGT, 12 November), targeting cloud-hosted ConnectWise ScreenConnect instances. Huntress has identified six compromised MSPs and 286 affected endpoints across 47 organisations, and says the number of victims continues to rise. Attackers use ScreenConnect's Run Command functionality to deploy rogue ScreenConnect clients on managed endpoints, giving them remote access outside the legitimate MSP's ScreenConnect environment. Huntress also warned of a potentially more dangerous technique in which attackers may be able to compromise an MSP technician's workstation when the technician starts a ScreenConnect session with an infected customer device; it is unclear how this reverse-pivot technique works, including whether it exploits a software vulnerability or abuses legitimate functionality. Huntress has not determined how attackers first gain access to MSP environments, but says its telemetry points to compromised credentials and hijacked MSP support sessions, and that sequential attacker-assigned tags suggest other MSPs may have been compromised earlier. Huntress published indicators of compromise, including attacker relay 185.99.255.28 and rogue ScreenConnect client IDs 2588ef5c15954b10 and ed630cc2c873b091. ConnectWise confirmed it is investigating and urged partners to avoid interactive sessions with suspected compromised devices, review account activity, revoke active sessions, reset credentials from a trusted device and verify multi-factor authentication. In a Trust Center advisory at 22:45 UTC on 11 November, ConnectWise said it was aware of unauthorised access to partner accounts and the deployment of unauthorised remote-access software in customer environments, and disabled five third-party extensions (Labtech Plus, RMM Plus, RMM+, RMM Plus Password Link and RMM+ Password Link) in about 400 partner environments as a precaution. BleepingComputer found an earlier malicious batch script referencing one of the rogue client IDs, uploaded to VirusTotal on 25 July 2026; it is unclear whether that activity is part of the same campaign. The Hacker News reported on 12 November that the count had risen to at least 288 endpoints across 48 organisations, and that ConnectWise said there was no evidence the incident involved a compromise of its own infrastructure.
entries.source_name: BleepingComputer, 11 November 2026; Huntress; ConnectWise Trust Center; The Hacker News, 12 November 2026
entries.summary: An active campaign discovered by Huntress on 11 November 2026 is compromising managed service providers' cloud-hosted ConnectWise ScreenConnect environments and using them to deploy rogue remote-access clients on customer devices: six MSPs and 286 endpoints across 47 organisations are confirmed affected so far, with numbers rising. ConnectWise is investigating and has disabled five third-party extensions in about 400 partner environments as a precaution. The initial access route is undetermined, and no ransomware payload has been reported yet.
entries.type: Active campaign — MSP remote-access abuse
entries.unknown: How attackers first gain access to MSP environments; whether the July 2026 activity using one of the rogue client IDs is part of the same campaign; how the reported reverse-pivot technique works and whether it relies on a vulnerability or on legitimate functionality; whether ransomware or other payloads will be deployed through the rogue clients; the full count of compromised MSPs.

entries.bfsi_impact: The Arara breach keeps widening across Japanese financial firms: MUFG and Nomura are the latest named victims, and any bank or insurer that used Arara Message — directly or through a contractor such as GiftPad — should assume shareholder or customer email addresses may be exposed and warn them about phishing impersonating the firm. The pattern also shows a single email-delivery supplier can expose hundreds of clients at once, so firms should inventory which suppliers hold their customer contact data.
entries.headline: MUFG and Nomura Holdings disclose shareholder email leaks via Arara breach
entries.known: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG) said on 11 November 2026 that email addresses of 20,000 shareholders had leaked after unauthorised access to Arara's Arara Message email-delivery service; the affected shareholders were those who received e-gift winning emails in July 2026. Nomura Holdings disclosed the same day that 13,500 shareholder email addresses had leaked the same way. Both firms outsource e-gift operations to GiftPad, which used Arara's service. No shareholder numbers or email contents were included, and neither firm's own systems were breached. Arara has said up to about 81 million email addresses were exposed across roughly 380 corporate clients; its parent Paycloud put the figure at about 77 million on 2 November. Arara said attackers exploited vulnerabilities in its web servers on 28 October, and the Arara Message service has been suspended since 31 October. The Cabinet Office also disclosed on 11 November that 62,863 email addresses from its newsletters had leaked via Arara, and Sega disclosed 2,196,044 customer email addresses on 9 November. No misuse of the leaked data has been confirmed.
entries.source_name: Nikkei, 11 November 2026 (translated from Japanese); Yomiuri Shimbun, 11 November 2026 (translated from Japanese)
entries.summary: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group and Nomura Holdings said on 11 November 2026 that shareholder email addresses — 20,000 at MUFG and 13,500 at Nomura — had leaked through unauthorised access to email-delivery provider Arara's Arara Message service, via their shared e-gift contractor GiftPad. No shareholder numbers or email contents were included and neither firm's own systems were breached. Arara has said up to about 81 million email addresses were exposed across roughly 380 corporate clients.
entries.type: Confirmed breach — third-party email provider / named BFSI victims
entries.unknown: Whether any leaked addresses have been used in phishing; the full list of affected Arara clients; the exact intrusion route beyond Arara's statement that web-server vulnerabilities were exploited on 28 October.

entries.bfsi_impact: Accounting and advisory firms hold client tax, payroll and financial records including Social Security numbers, so a breach at a third-party platform they use is directly usable for identity theft and tax fraud against their clients. Peer firms should check whether they use the same unnamed provider, warn affected clients to watch for identity fraud and tax-refund scams, and review third-party platform access controls.
entries.headline: Baker Tilly notifies clients of data breach at third-party provider; Social Security numbers exposed
entries.known: Baker Tilly Advisory Group, a major US accounting, tax and advisory firm, is notifying clients and their dependents that a data breach compromised personal information held on a platform operated by a third-party service provider it uses to serve clients. The firm became aware of the incident on 6 September 2026 and completed its review of the affected data on 28 October, when it identified whose information was involved; notification letters are dated 9 November. The breach notice does not give a total count of affected clients, does not name the provider and leaves the specific data types as a placeholder, but the Texas Attorney General's breach portal lists 10,456 affected Texas residents with Social Security numbers, full names, addresses and other information exposed; law-firm trackers also cite 2,689 affected in Massachusetts and over 500 in California. Baker Tilly says it contained the incident, engaged external experts, notified law enforcement and found no evidence of unauthorised activity on its own network. No ransomware group has claimed the attack.
entries.source_name: BleepingComputer, 11 November 2026; Texas Attorney General data security breach portal
entries.summary: Baker Tilly Advisory Group, a major US accounting, tax and advisory firm, is notifying clients that a data breach at a third-party service provider exposed client personal information including Social Security numbers. The firm learned of the incident on 6 September and finished its review on 28 October; at least 10,456 Texas residents are affected, with further victims in Massachusetts and California. The provider has not been named and no threat actor has claimed the attack.
entries.type: Confirmed breach — third-party provider / accounting firm
entries.unknown: The total number of affected clients has not been disclosed — only state-level figures (10,456 in Texas, 2,689 in Massachusetts, over 500 in California) are public. The third-party provider has not been named, the attack method and the attacker's identity are undisclosed, and it is not known when the intrusion began.

entries.bfsi_impact: If genuine, client investment portfolios, account records and corporate data at a publicly listed Kuwaiti investment firm managing about $4.3 billion would be at risk; firms with NIC exposure or Kuwaiti market counterparties should watch for a company statement and for any published data, and treat the claim as unverified until then. As a listed company on Boursa Kuwait, a confirmed incident could also raise disclosure questions.
entries.headline: The Gentlemen ransomware group claims Kuwait's National Investments Company as victim; claim unverified

NIC is a publicly listed Kuwaiti investment firm reportedly managing about $4.3 billion across investment, treasury, real estate and asset management. The listing gives no file count, data volume, downloadable samples or technical evidence, and NIC has not publicly confirmed any incident.
entries.source_name: Undercode News (citing Dark Web Intelligence), 11 November 2026
entries.summary: The Gentlemen ransomware group has listed Kuwait's National Investments Company, a publicly listed investment firm managing about $4.3 billion, on its leak site. No evidence, samples or company confirmation have been provided, so the claim remains unverified.

entries.unknown: Whether NIC was actually breached, what data if any was taken, and whether the group will publish anything. No company statement has been found, and the claim remains unverified.

entries.bfsi_impact: Banks and insurers running XCP-ng with an internet-exposed Xen Orchestra should patch immediately and hunt for the published indicators: the flaw gives unauthenticated admin access and full host takeover, and exploitation is already under way.
entries.headline: Critical Xen Orchestra authentication bypass actively exploited to hijack VM servers
entries.known: Vates disclosed and patched a critical authentication bypass (VSA-2026-062) in Xen Orchestra that is already being exploited: sending an empty-object authenticationToken cookie returns a valid admin token, giving full XCP-ng host takeover as root. No CVE has been assigned yet. The flaw is fixed in Xen Orchestra 6.9.2 (stable) / 6.10.1 (latest); early coverage cited 6.9.1/6.10.0 before the advisory was updated. Published indicators include 91.211.251.112:8001 (flagged as RedLine Stealer infrastructure), a Tor onion address and a VM named pivot2.
entries.source_name: Vates security advisory VSA-2026-062; BleepingComputer, 10 November 2026
entries.summary: Vates has disclosed a critical authentication bypass in Xen Orchestra (VSA-2026-062) that is already being exploited: an empty-object authentication cookie returns a valid admin token, allowing full XCP-ng host takeover as root. A fix is available in Xen Orchestra 6.9.1/6.10.0, and indicators of compromise have been published.
entries.type: Actively exploited vulnerability — virtualisation
entries.unknown: How many organisations have been compromised, and whether any financial-sector hosts are among them.

entries.bfsi_impact: The case shows government bank accounts being drained through a compromised transaction portal rather than phishing: banks and public bodies using the same online financial transaction portal should check access controls and transaction logs for unauthorised sessions.
entries.headline: Over Rs 22 crore siphoned from Tamil Nadu panchayat bank accounts in suspected cyber-fraud syndicate attack
entries.known: More than Rs 22 crore (about US$2.5 million) was siphoned from Tamil Nadu panchayat bank accounts after unauthorised access to the online financial transaction portal: Rs 14 crore from Mandapam, Rs 3.1 crore from Nagapattinam and Rs 5 crore from Dharapuram. Chennai Central Crime Branch has registered a case and police suspect an international cyber-fraud syndicate.
entries.source_name: ThePrint (PTI), 10 November 2026
entries.summary: More than Rs 22 crore (about US$2.5 million) was siphoned from Tamil Nadu panchayat bank accounts — Rs 14 crore from Mandapam, Rs 3.1 crore from Nagapattinam and Rs 5 crore from Dharapuram — after unauthorised access to the online financial transaction portal. Chennai police suspect an international cyber-fraud syndicate.
entries.type: Payment fraud — unauthorised transfers
entries.unknown: How the attackers accessed the transaction portal, whether any funds have been recovered, and whether the suspected syndicate is confirmed.

entries.bfsi_impact: Banks, payment firms and crypto-facing institutions should screen for MEXC exposure, warn customers and counterparties that transfers to or from MEXC now carry secondary-sanctions risk, and treat the $16 billion figure as a reminder that exchanges with weak anti-money-laundering controls remain a conduit for ransomware and scam proceeds.
entries.headline: US Treasury cuts off MEXC crypto exchange over $16 billion in illicit transactions
entries.known: The US Treasury Department, through a Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) order issued 6 November 2026, cut off Seychelles-based MEXC Global from the US financial system. FinCEN said MEXC allowed illicit transactions of at least $16 billion linked to cybercrime operations and Iranian, North Korean and Russian sanctions evasion between May 2021 and May 2026. The Treasury said MEXC was still processing transactions with sanctioned Russian entities Garantex and Grinex as recently as June 2026, facilitated or processed at least $226 million in transactions connected to the OFAC-sanctioned A7 sanctions-evasion network, and sent or received about $1 billion in direct transactions with more than 40 identified Iranian crypto exchangers, some under US and international sanctions. FinCEN blamed deficiencies in MEXC's anti-money-laundering and customer identification policies. The ban exposes US financial institutions and individuals to secondary sanctions or enforcement action for transfers to or from MEXC. MEXC, one of the world's largest crypto exchanges with more than 40 million users in over 170 countries, said it is operating normally, that user assets remain secure, and that it has begun an independent review of its AML and sanctions controls.
entries.source_name: BleepingComputer, 9 November 2026
entries.summary: The US Treasury Department, via a FinCEN order issued 6 November 2026, cut off crypto exchange MEXC Global from the US financial system, saying it allowed at least $16 billion in illicit transactions linked to cybercrime and Iranian, North Korean and Russian sanctions evasion between May 2021 and May 2026. MEXC says it is operating normally and is reviewing its anti-money-laundering controls.
entries.type: Regulatory enforcement — exchange cut off from US financial system
entries.unknown: Whether MEXC will challenge the order, what happens to US users' funds and access, and whether other regulators follow with their own action.

entries.bfsi_impact: Small credit unions are a soft target for ransomware groups: the exposed Social Security numbers, government IDs and account and card numbers are directly usable for identity theft and account fraud. Peer credit unions should check their own exposure to the Storm group's claimed access pattern and warn affected members to watch for identity fraud. The 656 figure covers Texas residents only; the total affected population has not been stated.
entries.headline: Insight Credit Union discloses breach affecting 656 Texans after Storm ransomware group claimed attack
entries.known: Insight Credit Union, a state-chartered credit union headquartered in Winter Springs, Florida, disclosed a data breach exposing names, Social Security numbers, driver's licence numbers, other government-issued ID numbers such as passport or state ID numbers, and financial information including account numbers and credit or debit card numbers. The credit union reported the breach to the Texas attorney general on 6 November 2026, identifying 656 affected Texas residents. On 15 September 2026 the ransomware group Storm posted a claim on the dark web saying it had breached the credit union, had obtained 209 gigabytes of data and intended to publish it within 17 days.
entries.source_name: teiss, 9 November 2026
entries.summary: Insight Credit Union, a state-chartered credit union in Winter Springs, Florida, disclosed a data breach exposing names, Social Security numbers, driver's licence numbers, other government IDs and financial account and card numbers. It reported the breach to the Texas attorney general on 6 November 2026, identifying 656 affected Texas residents. The ransomware group Storm claimed on 15 September 2026 to have breached the credit union and taken 209 GB of data.
entries.type: Confirmed disclosure — ransomware claim
entries.unknown: Whether Storm was responsible for the breach has not been independently confirmed — the link rests on the group's dark-web claim. The credit union has not said when the intrusion occurred, how the attackers got in, or whether the 209 GB claimed by Storm matches what was taken. The total number of affected members beyond Texas has not been stated.

entries.bfsi_impact: A financial regulator confirming exposure of platform users' tax IDs and contact details is a direct identity-fraud enabler: names, mobile numbers, birth dates, addresses and TINs can be used for impersonation and phishing against investors and corporate filers. Peer regulators and firms running investor or filing portals should warn users to change reused passwords, enable multi-factor authentication and treat any message citing their SEC account details as suspect, and should check whether their own user data sits in similarly exposed portal datasets.
entries.headline: Philippine SEC confirms breach of platform users; names, contact details and tax IDs exposed
entries.known: The Philippine Securities and Exchange Commission confirmed on 9 November 2026 that personal information belonging to users of its online platforms was exposed, and sent direct notifications to affected account holders the same day. The exposed data is limited to full names, usernames, email addresses, mobile numbers, dates of birth, genders, physical addresses and Tax Identification Numbers (TINs). The SEC said the leak may have originated from malware infections or unauthorised third-party access targeting the devices users used to log into its portals, and said passwords stored in its databases were not leaked, corporate filings were unaffected and no system data was altered or destroyed. The SEC reported the incident to the National Privacy Commission and advised users to change passwords reused elsewhere, enable multi-factor authentication and scan their devices. The confirmation followed a preliminary advisory on 7 November, after the SEC became aware on 6 November of online reports alleging a database linked to the agency had leaked; cybersecurity advocacy group Deep Web Konek had flagged a possible breach of SEC-related accounts days before the 9 November advisory.
entries.source_name: BitPinas, 9 November 2026; SEC Philippines advisory on X, 9 November 2026
entries.summary: The Philippine Securities and Exchange Commission confirmed on 9 November 2026 that personal information of users of its online platforms - names, usernames, email addresses, mobile numbers, dates of birth, genders, addresses and Tax Identification Numbers - was exposed, and notified affected account holders directly. The SEC said the leak may have come from malware or third-party access on users' own devices, that no passwords in its databases leaked, and that corporate filings were unaffected. The number of affected users has not been disclosed.
entries.type: Confirmed breach - financial regulator / platform users
entries.unknown: How many users are affected has not been disclosed. The SEC has not said how it determined the likely origin was users' devices, and the investigation is still verifying the origin, scope and validity of the dataset. Whether any exposed data has been misused has not been reported.

entries.bfsi_impact: Financial firms in Southeast Asia should hunt for the eight published IP indicators and for the behavioural pattern Microsoft describes — bursts of varied requests against internet-facing systems, SSRF and anonymous file-upload exploitation, and curl/netcat downloads of RATs — and check cloud-identity and Entra ID sign-in activity. The campaign shows AI-agent tooling moving from state-aligned actors to financially motivated crime against banks, so controls that assume a human-speed attacker, including fingerprint-based blocking alone, are not enough.
entries.headline: Microsoft: financially motivated Storm-3358 using ARTEX AI framework against financial firms in Southeast Asia
entries.known: Microsoft observed Storm-3358 combining ARTEX with conventional automated tools to scan internet-facing systems, exploit flaws including anonymous file upload and server-side request forgery (SSRF), and install open-source remote access trojans (WISP, vshell and AdaptixC2) for persistence and lateral movement; ARTEX agents used netcat and curl to download the RATs. The activity was observed from early October through early November 2026. Exposed surfaces include internet-facing web applications and servers, cloud identities, and identity and sign-in systems including Microsoft Entra ID. Microsoft published eight IP addresses as ARTEX servers, command-and-control infrastructure or WISP nodes and said most were still active on 6 November, while warning that attackers use proxies and VPNs to change source addresses. Microsoft says blocking the tools' default traffic fingerprints alone will not stop an AI agent, which changes them quickly, and recommends hunting on behaviour — high volumes of varied requests, retried technique variations and unusually fast progression between attack stages. This widens ARTEX abuse beyond the state-aligned Storm-0940 activity Microsoft reported earlier; ARTEX is already tracked in the Storm-0940/ARTEX deep-research page.
entries.source_name: Microsoft Security Blog, 6 November 2026
entries.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence said on 6 November 2026 that the financially motivated, Cambodia-based intrusion cluster Storm-3358 began targeting financial organisations in Southeast Asia in October 2026 using the agentic AI offensive framework ARTEX, exploiting flaws such as anonymous file upload and server-side request forgery and installing the WISP, vshell and AdaptixC2 remote access trojans. Microsoft published eight IP indicators, most still active on 6 November. No victims were named and no victim count given.
entries.type: Ongoing campaign — AI-driven attacks on financial sector
entries.unknown: No victim institution was named and no count of intrusions or losses was given. Whether any of the observed intrusions reached data exfiltration or fund movement has not been reported.

entries.bfsi_impact: Banks, card issuers and payment firms should treat the pairing of a named person with home address, card number and wallet addresses as durable targeting data for phishing and impersonation — the wallet link does not expire when the card retires on 20 December. Customers of crypto-linked card products should be warned against fake 'migrate your account' messages citing real purchase or address details, and that no legitimate message will ask for a seed phrase, private key, PIN or full card number. The June incident at the same product shows a repeat-exposure pattern worth noting in third-party risk reviews of crypto card providers.
entries.headline: Gnosis Pay confirms breach of legacy consumer card system; card numbers and wallet addresses exposed
entries.known: Gnosis Pay said its monitoring detected unauthorised access on 3 November 2026 to the system powering its Gnosis Pay-branded cards (its consumer business), with containment starting within two hours; the affected credentials were replaced and the vulnerability addressed. The breach was limited to that system, which was already scheduled for retirement on 20 December 2026; the enterprise platform running white-label card programmes was not affected. The cards are Visa debit cards issued by Monavate, an e-money firm authorised by the UK Financial Conduct Authority. The company emailed every affected customer a list of exactly what was taken from their account, reported the breach to its partners, data protection authorities and its card issuer, made 3D Secure mandatory for all online card payments, and stepped up fraud monitoring. One customer's notice, shared publicly by Rotki founder Lefteris Karapetsas and reported by CoinDesk, listed his name, full home address, card number and every wallet address linked to his account. This is the card product's second security incident this year: in June attackers exploited a flaw in wallet software modules used by Gnosis Pay accounts and extracted about $1.5 million, which Gnosis absorbed and restored.
entries.source_name: Gnosis Pay disclosure, 6 November 2026; Coindoo, 8 November 2026
entries.summary: Crypto payments firm Gnosis Pay said on 6 November 2026 that unauthorised access detected on 3 November to the system behind its own-branded Visa debit cards exposed customer information, including card numbers, home addresses and linked wallet addresses for at least one customer. Customer funds were not affected and the enterprise white-label platform was not hit. The number of affected customers has not been disclosed; the consumer card system is due to retire on 20 December 2026.
entries.type: Confirmed breach — crypto payments / card issuer
entries.unknown: Gnosis Pay has not disclosed how many customers were affected, when the intrusion began (3 November is only the detection date), or whether exposed card data included expiry dates or security codes. Whether any exposed data has been misused has not been reported; the company says it has arranged specialist monitoring for signs of misuse.

entries.bfsi_impact: If genuine, the exposure of PAN, Aadhaar and account numbers for millions of customers would be directly usable for identity fraud and impersonation against the bank's customers. Peer banks using third-party SaaS platforms for customer onboarding should check what data sits with vendors and how it is accessed. Until verified, treat this as an unconfirmed claim, not a confirmed breach — the bank's position remains that only a limited third-party platform leak occurred.
entries.headline: Threat actor claims 1.2 TB AU Small Finance Bank database for sale; bank has not responded to new claim
entries.known: The actor's forum post, as reported by Digit.in, claims the stolen data includes PAN and Aadhaar numbers, dates of birth, mobile numbers, email addresses and residential addresses, plus nearly 3.9 million KYC identity records and over 2.2 million active customer account records, and alleges the bank's own core systems were breached. The claim directly contradicts the bank's late-October statement, which attributed the incident to a limited leak from a third-party Salesforce-hosted SaaS platform holding vehicle-loan customer data and said its own systems were unaffected. The bank said on 30 October it was investigating, had informed the Reserve Bank of India and CERT-In, and that a forensic investigation was under way. Salesforce said on 31 October it had found no platform vulnerability linked to the claims. On 12 November, RDU Global reported that the bank is now investigating a possible limited data breach involving vehicle-loan customer data held on a Salesforce-hosted third-party platform.
entries.source_name: Digit.in, 7 November 2026; ThreatMon on X, 6 November 2026; RDU Global, 12 November 2026
entries.summary: A threat actor claims to have stolen 1.2 TB of data from India's AU Small Finance Bank — over 1 billion records, including more than 2.2 million live customer accounts and over 1.9 million bank account numbers — and is offering it for sale for US$8,500. The claim, flagged by threat-intelligence account ThreatMon on X on 6 November and reported by Digit.in on 7 November, has not been independently verified, and the bank has not yet commented on it.
entries.type: Unverified leak claim — named BFSI victim
entries.unknown: The claim has not been independently verified, no data sample has been publicly authenticated, and the bank has not responded to the new claim. Whether the data offered for sale is genuine, how it was obtained, and how many customers are actually affected are all unconfirmed.

entries.bfsi_impact: A ransomware listing against a US insurer is a watch item for the sector even while unverified: peer insurers should check for any exposure to the same group and watch for confirmation or a data publication. Until verified, treat this as an unconfirmed claim, not a confirmed breach.
entries.headline: Metaencryptor ransomware group claims Pekin Insurance as victim; claim unverified
entries.known: Ransomware.live recorded the listing on 7 November 2026 at 11:39 UTC. The listing was flagged by the ThreatMon threat-intelligence team the same day. Pekin Insurance is a group of combined entities including The Farmers Automobile Insurance Association, Pekin Insurance Company, Pekin Select Insurance Company and Pekin Life Insurance Company. Hudson Rock infostealer data linked to the organisation shows 849 exposed passwords, 39 of them critical, and 10 cookies, though that exposure is not itself evidence of the ransomware claim.
entries.source_name: Ransomware.live, 7 November 2026; QPulse, 7 November 2026
entries.summary: The Metaencryptor ransomware group listed US insurer Pekin Insurance as a victim on its leak site on 7 November 2026. No independently verified evidence of data theft, encryption or operational disruption has been provided, and Pekin Insurance has not publicly confirmed the claim.
entries.type: Unverified ransomware claim — named BFSI victim
entries.unknown: No independently verified information has been provided about the alleged intrusion, the nature of any compromised data, or any impact on customers or operations. Pekin Insurance has not publicly confirmed the claim, and no ransom demand or data sample has been publicly reported.

entries.bfsi_impact: If genuine, the publication of more than 217,000 client policy and underwriting documents exposes brokerage clients to identity theft and targeted phishing using real policy numbers and producer data. Insurers and brokerages should treat the N0n leak as a prompt to audit access controls on document stores and CRM systems, and to watch for phishing using the exposed client and producer details. Until verified, treat this as an unconfirmed claim, not a confirmed breach.
entries.headline: N0n ransomware group publishes 217,000+ documents from insurance brokerage Higginbotham; firm has not confirmed breach
entries.known: Ransomware.live recorded the leak-site listing on 7 November 2026 at 10:53 UTC. The posting describes the complete correspondence attachment store of the brokerage: over 217,000 client policy and working documents from 2013 through 2026, including workers compensation and property policies of named clients, carrier underwriting questionnaires, producer reports with client codes, names and policy numbers, producer emails with commission, prospect and benefits data, client reference rosters, producer books of business with policy numbers and premiums, and the full customer relationship databases. The listing is marked 'NOT PAID — EXPOSED', indicating the data was published after no ransom was paid.
entries.source_name: Ransomware.live, 7 November 2026; QPulse, 7 November 2026
entries.summary: The N0n ransomware group published data it claims was stolen from Higginbotham, a large independent US insurance brokerage, listing the material as 'NOT PAID — EXPOSED'. The posting describes over 217,000 client policy and working documents from 2013–2026, including workers' compensation and property policies, underwriting questionnaires, producer reports with client codes, names and policy numbers, and full customer-relationship databases. Higginbotham has not publicly confirmed the breach.
entries.type: Unverified leak publication — named BFSI victim
entries.unknown: Higginbotham has not publicly confirmed the incident, and the stolen data has not been independently verified. It is not publicly known when the unauthorised access occurred or how the attackers entered the brokerage's systems.

entries.bfsi_impact: A second-day trading and withdrawal freeze at a Binance-backed exchange, in the middle of South Korea's financial-sector breach wave, is a confidence signal for the sector even without a confirmed intrusion. Banks and payment firms with crypto-adjacent exposure should watch for a resumption date and for any confirmation of the threat, and treat the unverified claim as a prompt to check their own incident-response readiness rather than as a confirmed breach.
entries.headline: Gopax freezes trading and withdrawals after hacking-threat email; threat unverified
entries.known: Gopax halted withdrawals at 14:55 on 6 November and trading at 15:53, cancelling all unfilled orders, and also suspended virtual-asset deposits. Standard withdrawals through the website and app are disabled; customers can request withdrawals through customer support, processed manually after internal review. The exchange said it acted on the advice of financial regulators amid the wave of breaches across the sector, and that no customer assets have been lost so far. Gopax is majority-owned by Binance, and its operator Streami was among the 16 firms in the Financial Services Commission's 14 October disclosure of breaches, having reported exposure of seven customers and two current or former employees.
entries.source_name: Aju Press, 7 November 2026; Korea JoongAng Daily, 7 November 2026
entries.summary: South Korean cryptocurrency exchange Gopax suspended deposits, withdrawals and trading on 6 November 2026 after receiving a threatening email from a party claiming to have hacked the platform, and the freeze was still in place on the morning of 7 November with no date set for resuming services. The exchange says it has not verified the threat and has detected no hacking attempt or asset loss; it is moving customer assets to offline cold wallets as a precaution.
entries.type: Service suspension — crypto exchange, unverified threat
entries.unknown: Whether the hacking threat is genuine has not been confirmed, and no intrusion or theft has been detected. When normal trading, deposits and withdrawals will resume has not been announced.

entries.bfsi_impact: Brazilian banks, brokerages and investment platforms should warn clients holding guaranteed investments about phishing that uses the exposed data — for example messages claiming a guarantee payment is waiting and demanding a fee. The victim here is the guarantee fund itself, so peers should also check whether their own customer data sits in shared guarantee-payment workflows and how access to those environments is controlled.
entries.headline: Brazil's FGC deposit guarantee fund confirms unauthorised access to investor data
entries.known: FGC (Fundo Garantidor de Créditos), Brazil's deposit guarantee fund, said in an official statement dated 5 November 2026 that unauthorised access to personal data was identified on 26 October 2026 in environments connected to its payment-guarantee processes. The exposed data includes names, CPF tax identification numbers, email addresses and dates of birth, plus guarantee-payment details such as tax withheld on payments and the distribution channel through which the guaranteed investment was made. FGC says there is no evidence the data was disclosed or misused and no financial loss from the event, and the investigation continues with specialist firms. Brazil's National Data Protection Authority (ANPD) and the affected individuals have been notified.
entries.source_name: FGC official statement, 5 November 2026 (translated from Portuguese); InfoMoney, 5 November 2026
entries.summary: Brazil's Fundo Garantidor de Créditos (FGC), the deposit guarantee fund, disclosed on 5 November 2026 that unauthorised access to personal data in its payment-guarantee environments was identified on 26 October. Names, CPF tax IDs, email addresses and dates of birth were exposed, along with guarantee-payment details. FGC says there is no evidence of misuse or financial loss and the investigation continues; Brazil's data protection authority (ANPD) has been notified.
entries.type: Confirmed breach — deposit guarantee fund
entries.unknown: FGC has not said how many people are affected, how the attackers gained access, or whether the data was copied; the investigation is still establishing the extent of the access.

entries.bfsi_impact: Moldovan banks face a wave of impersonation fraud: real names, family data, IBANs and bank account numbers let scammers pose convincingly as bank or government staff. Banks elsewhere should treat this as a reminder that a government-register breach is a fraud enabler even without direct account compromise — warn customers never to share passwords or authentication codes by phone or message, and watch for phishing that cites genuine personal details. The National Bank of Moldova says banking systems were not compromised.
entries.headline: Moldova government breach exposes data of 450,000 citizens, including IBANs and bank account numbers
entries.known: President Maia Sandu confirmed on 6 November, after a National Security Council meeting, that a cyberattack on systems run by the Electronic Governance Agency exposed personal data of about 450,000 citizens — close to a fifth of the population. The intrusion ran 19–23 October: a flaw meant the systems checked which application requested data but not the identity of the user or whether they were authorised, and attackers made about 11 million access requests from more than 638 IP addresses, querying about one million personal identification numbers. Data from at least ten public institutions was accessed, including names, family records, health and pension data, and financial data: IBANs, bank account numbers, tax debts and MPay payment histories. An initial estimate of about 750,000 affected was revised down to about 450,000. Sandu said no bank data had been used to access citizens' accounts, and that banks will be told which citizens' data was consulted. The Chișinău prosecutor's office has opened a criminal investigation.
entries.source_name: Moldova Live, 6 November 2026; Radio Moldova, 6 November 2026
entries.summary: Moldova's president confirmed on 6 November that a cyberattack on the Electronic Governance Agency's systems exposed personal data of about 450,000 citizens, including IBANs, bank account numbers, tax debts and payment histories. The attack ran 19–23 October via a flaw that verified the requesting application but not the user. The president said no bank data had been used to access citizens' accounts and that banking systems were not compromised; the risk is impersonation fraud using the exposed personal and banking details.
entries.type: Government data breach — financial data exposed
entries.unknown: The attackers have not been publicly identified. The government suspects a state-sponsored operation but has presented no conclusive public evidence and has not attributed the attack to any country. Whether the exposed data has been misused has not been reported, and the full list of affected institutions has not been published.

entries.bfsi_impact: Chainalysis KYT and address screening are used by banks, exchanges and payment firms for crypto transaction monitoring and sanctions screening. With KYT and the login portal offline and all users required to reset passwords and rotate API keys, firms relying on Chainalysis screening face disrupted transaction monitoring and should treat any Chainalysis-branded password-reset or support message as suspect, since exposed names, roles and live tokens enable convincing impersonation of compliance staff and customers. No investigative graph data or attribution data is reported accessed, so the direct risk is credential and session abuse, not corrupted blockchain attribution.
entries.headline: Chainalysis says breach exposed credentials and live tokens for all customers; KYT screening taken offline
entries.known: Chainalysis first disclosed on 30 October that an attacker using what it called 'offensive agentic techniques' accessed customer names, email addresses, user IDs and organisation role labels, initially described as non-sensitive identity metadata. In updates on 4 November the company said an 'on-path' (man-in-the-middle) attack had exposed a subset of customer passwords and it locked affected accounts. In a further update at 23:00 ET on 4 November it said it had discovered on Monday 2 November that names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all Chainalysis users were exposed to a malicious actor. The company took its login portal offline, together with Reactor, Data Solutions, the Know-Your-Transaction (KYT) user interface and API, and address-screening products, after detecting further abnormal activity, and asked customers to supply trusted IP addresses for an allowlist before resetting passwords and rotating API keys. On 6 November it began restoring KYT and address screening in phases; Reactor and Data Solutions remained offline. The company says it has no evidence investigative graph data was accessed or attribution data manipulated, and that the incident is unrelated to the Binance theft. On 7 November the company said Reactor, KYT (user interface and API) and address screening were back online with enhanced security, with customers being reconnected in phases; Data Solutions and Chain (Beta) remained offline with no return date given.
entries.source_name: BleepingComputer, 6 November 2026 (company incident-page updates); company incident page, 7 November 2026; TokenPost, 8 November 2026
entries.summary: Blockchain-intelligence firm Chainalysis widened its account of its late-October breach: names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all customers were exposed, and its KYT transaction-screening service and login portal were taken offline. Financial institutions using Chainalysis for crypto screening face disrupted monitoring and a phishing and impersonation risk from the exposed credentials.
entries.type: Supplier breach — crypto compliance and screening vendor
entries.unknown: How the attacker got in, which internal tools were reached, how long they had access, and how many organisations are affected have not been disclosed. The attacker is not identified. It is not yet clear how many KYT accounts were accessed without authorisation; Chainalysis says it is directly notifying affected customers.

entries.bfsi_impact: Regulator outreach signals official concern that crypto-market incidents can ripple into traditional finance. Banks should expect follow-up questions on crypto-adjacent exposures and be ready to evidence their own checks after the Binance hack.
entries.headline: US regulators contact banks to check systems after $6.34bn Binance hack
entries.known: Reuters reported that supervisors from the US Federal Reserve and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency began contacting banks on Monday morning to ask whether they had detected unusual activity or service disruptions after the $6.34 billion Binance hack of 29 October. A US bank official who received the inquiry said the institution had experienced no significant service disruptions. US banks are conducting their own system reviews, and one of the largest US banks contacted Binance's security personnel directly within hours of the hack. South Korea's Financial Services Commission held an emergency meeting on Monday with the Financial Supervisory Service, the Korea Financial Security Institute, the Digital Asset eXchange Alliance and major virtual-asset service providers to review access controls, wallet withdrawal approval and signing procedures, and administrator privilege management.
entries.source_name: Korea Herald Business, 6 November 2026, citing Reuters
entries.summary: US financial regulators have begun contacting banks to check for unusual activity or service disruptions after the $6.34 billion Binance hack of 29 October; no bank has reported a disruption. South Korea's Financial Services Commission held an emergency meeting with crypto exchanges on Monday to review security controls.
entries.type: Sector alert — regulator response
entries.unknown: Which banks were contacted and what, if anything, was found have not been reported. No bank has reported a disruption linked to the Binance hack.

entries.bfsi_impact: If genuine, a US private bank's customer and signer records held by its analytics vendor are exposed. Peer banks should check what client data sits with analytics and AI vendors, review vendor access and exfiltration controls, and watch for phishing or impersonation using signer and account details. Until verified, treat this as an unconfirmed claim, not a confirmed breach.
entries.headline: N0n ransomware group claims Scry Analytics leak exposed US private-banking client records
entries.known: The N0n extortion group listed Scry Analytics, a US data-analytics and AI services firm, on its leak site; the listing was discovered on 6 November at 01:22 UTC (09:22 SGT). The post claims the exposed material includes core banking customer and signer records of a US private banking client — names, account records, signer roles, addresses and contact details — plus a global insurance group's party master of 7,904 legal-entity records with relationship structures, and production support-call transcripts and recordings containing consumer names and mobile numbers. The post says the data was held under contract and marks it 'not paid — exposed'. No ransom amount is stated and no encryption is claimed.
entries.source_name: ransomware.live / RedPacket Security, 6 November 2026 (leak-site listing, unconfirmed)
entries.summary: The N0n extortion group claims a leak from US analytics firm Scry Analytics exposed core customer and signer records of a US private banking client, plus an insurance group's party master of 7,904 records and support-call recordings. The claim rests on the group's own leak-site post only — neither Scry Analytics nor the bank has confirmed it — so it is carried here as reported / unconfirmed.
entries.type: Unverified leak-site claim — third-party data exposure
entries.unknown: The private banking client is not named. There is no confirmation from Scry Analytics or the bank, and no independent verification that the data was exfiltrated or is genuine. The compromise date and method are not stated — the post date is not the compromise date.

entries.bfsi_impact: Banks, payment aggregators and fintech partners with Indian operations or Indian payment-API exposure should check API inventories, shut down dormant or test interfaces, enforce beneficiary verification and cooling periods, and flag ₹1-scale test transfers to new beneficiaries followed by larger transfers. ARTEX is already tracked in the Storm-0940/ARTEX deep-research page.
entries.headline: CERT-In warns India's BFSI sector of escalating AI-driven ‘Crafty Falcon’ payment-API attacks
entries.known: The advisory, issued 4 November and reported widely on 5 November, updates CERT-In's 9 October advisory on payment and disbursement API abuse. CERT-In's CSIRT-Fin says successful attacks continue to be reported, including by NBFCs and fintech firms that had already received earlier restricted advisories and taken remedial measures, and that remediated entities have been deliberately re-targeted after incomplete remediation. Attackers use publicly available AI-driven tools — ARTEX, PentAGI, Cairn and CyberStrikeAI — to survey targets, generate tailored attack scripts and execute full attack chains at machine speed, invoking victims' own payment and disbursement APIs to move funds to mule accounts, after testing routes with micro-value transactions as small as ₹1. Merchant settlement APIs were abused and cryptocurrency wallet keys stolen. Attacks were timed to coincide with weekends and public holidays. CERT-In advised 24x7 monitoring, API inventories with dormant interfaces shut down, beneficiary-name verification and cooling periods for new beneficiaries.
entries.source_name: Indian Express, 5 November 2026; PTI via Rediff, 4 November 2026
entries.summary: India's CERT-In issued an advisory on 4 November 2026 naming the AI-assisted threat actor CRAFTY FALCON and warning that attacks abusing banks', NBFCs' and fintech firms' own payment and disbursement APIs for unauthorised fund transfers are active, ongoing and escalating.
entries.type: Sector alert — national CERT
entries.unknown: No individual victim institution was named in the public reporting of the advisory, and no aggregate loss figure for the current escalation was published. Whether any affected entity is a bank with Singapore or APAC operations beyond India is not stated.

entries.bfsi_impact: APAC banks and firms with Korean operations should watch the FSC inspection programme and the planned CEO-accountability measures; the wave shows small virtual-asset and electronic-payment firms are the weakest link, and leaked personal data may feed voice-phishing against bank customers.
entries.headline: South Korea regulator discloses 40 breaches at 37 financial firms; sector-wide inspections ordered
entries.known: The Financial Services Commission announced the measures on 5 November at an industry-wide forum chaired by Chairman Lee Eok-won, attended by the Financial Supervisory Service and the Korea Financial Security Institute. No individual users have yet suffered direct financial losses, and no account passwords that could enable fraudulent transactions were confirmed among the leaked data. The FSC will inspect about 580 financial entities by year-end, plans to lift network-separation rules, launch an AI-based security framework, and draft a Digital Finance Safety Act by the first quarter of 2027. The incidents include previously reported breaches at brokerages, insurers and virtual-asset firms. As of 8 November, Korean press reported the count of firms with confirmed incidents had risen to 38, with about 510,000 records leaked (Hankook Ilbo, 8 November 2026).
entries.source_name: Korea Herald, 5 November 2026
entries.summary: South Korea's Financial Services Commission said 40 cybersecurity incidents were reported at 37 financial firms between 30 September and 5 November 2026, exposing about 473,000 records at that point (about 510,000 by 8 November, per Korean press), with about ₩1 billion (about US$746,000) stolen from company-managed funds at some electronic financial service providers, virtual asset businesses and P2P lenders.
entries.type: Sector alert — regulator response
entries.unknown: The FSC has not named all 37 firms or broken down the 40 incidents by firm, and whether any leaked data is exploited in secondary crime such as voice phishing remains unconfirmed.
